packages.title: GDPR data subject requests
packages.summary: Handle access, erasure and other privacy requests: statutory deadline, identity check, search of CRM, billing and support, erasure, and a DPO-approved reply.
packages.description:
GDPR data subject requests takes a privacy request from receipt to response inside the statutory deadline. The privacy team (or your web form posting to the API) fills in the start form: who is asking, their email, the request type (access, erasure, rectification, portability, objection), the jurisdiction and the date it arrived.

The Statutory deadlines decision table sets the response deadline and whether it can be extended (one month under EU and UK GDPR, 45 days under CCPA, 15 days for a CCPA opt-out) and the run gets an SLA to match. The request is added to the DSAR register and nothing is searched until the privacy team has verified the requester's identity; they can ask for more information or reject the request. Once verified, the CRM, billing system and support desk are searched by email, and for erasure requests an erasure is requested in each system, with any records kept by law listed.

The DPO reviews a drafted response with everything found, edits and approves it or sends it back, and the approved response is emailed to the requester and the register row closed. Adapt the deadline rules to your legal advice and the three system references to the systems that hold personal data.
packages.start: Starts from a form: the privacy team fills in the request from the Run dialog, or your privacy web form posts it to the start API or an inbound webhook.

changelog.notes: Uses the new forms: a themed start form with a grid and header, Verified / Need more info / Reject buttons on identity verification, Approve response / Send back on the DPO review, each with a grid and header.

setup: CRM, Billing system and Support desk integrations: set each base URL and API token. Each has a search reference (GET with ?email=) and an erasure reference (POST /erasure-requests); adjust paths and response models to your systems in Integrations, or remove a system you do not use.
Assignees: pick the privacy officer who verifies identity and revises responses, and the DPO who approves them (runs can pass privacy_officer_id and dpo_id).
Review the Statutory deadlines rules with your legal team; add rows for other jurisdictions you serve.
Optional: create an inbound webhook for the workflow so your privacy web form can submit requests directly.
Email: configure EMAIL_PROVIDER on the instance so requesters receive the identity request and the response (the steps continue on error).

packages.title: Inventory reorder
packages.summary: A daily stock check finds items at or below their reorder point, raises an Approve order / Skip task for each and emails the supplier a purchase order.
packages.description:
Inventory reorder keeps consumables and packaging from running out without anyone watching a spreadsheet. The Stock items table lists each item with its on-hand quantity, reorder point, reorder quantity, unit cost, supplier, supplier email, lead time and whether it is already on order. Sample rows cover packaging, labels, gloves, wipes, paper and toner, three of them below their reorder point.

Every morning at 07:00 the Daily stock check lists the active items and loops over them. Each item at or below its reorder point that is not already on order starts the Raise reorder sub-workflow: it marks the item on order, logs the reorder in the Reorders table with its estimated cost and gives the buyer a task with Approve order and Skip buttons. Approve order lets the buyer adjust the quantity, records the expected delivery date from the supplier's lead time and emails the purchase order to the supplier; Skip records why and releases the item so it comes up again tomorrow.

When anything was raised, the buyer also gets a short daily summary to confirm the stock counts are right before approving orders. No integrations needed.

Keep On hand up to date (edit the table, import a CSV or update it from another workflow). When stock arrives, untick On order.
Change the trigger time and time zone if 07:00 Pacific/Auckland does not suit, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER so purchase orders reach suppliers.

packages.title: Legal request intake & triage
packages.summary: One front door for NDAs, contract reviews, legal questions and disputes: a stepped intake form, routing to the right queue with an SLA, and a Data table for the legal team.
packages.description:
Legal request intake & triage gives the business one place to ask legal for help. People open the Legal request form page, four steps with a progress bar: About you, The request, Urgency, and Review & send. The questions change with the request type: an NDA asks who shares information and whose template, a contract review asks the contract type, value and whether personal data is involved, a legal question asks the area of law, and a dispute asks the amount and any deadline. People attach drafts, letters and the other side's paper, and pick an urgency and a needed-by date.

The form is in Application mode with its own Next, Back and Send to legal buttons, and its rules do the checking before anything reaches legal: a contract review must include the contract, High and Critical urgency need a reason (the field only appears then), the needed-by date cannot be in the past, and choosing a dispute raises the urgency to High with a short note.

Submitting starts the workflow. The Legal request routing decision table picks the queue (Commercial, Employment, Privacy & IP, Disputes or General counsel), the SLA in days and whether the general counsel reviews the outcome. The request is added to the Legal requests table, the requester gets an email with the reference and the date to expect an answer, and the lawyer gets a tabbed task: the request on one tab, their outcome on the other. They complete it, ask the requester for more information (the requester answers in their own task and it comes back) or decline it; high-value contracts, disputes and critical questions go to the general counsel before the requester hears back.

The legal team works from the Legal requests page: open requests sorted by SLA with type, urgency and status badges and relative due times, filters by type, status, queue and assignee, and a click on a row for the full details. Assignee and status can be changed in the table and saved back. Everything is built from forms, a decision table, a data table, emails and tasks: no integrations needed.

packages.title: Policy acknowledgement tracker
packages.summary: Every week, issue the current policy to every active person, track who has acknowledged it, remind the rest and give the policy owner one chase list.
packages.description:
Policy acknowledgement tracker turns "please read and confirm" emails into an auditable register. The Policy register table holds each policy, its version, link and whether staff must acknowledge it; the Staff table lists who has to confirm.

Every Monday at 09:00 the workflow picks the most recently effective current policy that needs acknowledging (or the one you name) and goes through every active person. Anyone not yet asked gets a Pending row in the Acknowledgements table, an email with the link and the deadline, and a tracker task (through a Record acknowledgement sub-workflow) where the policy owner records the confirmation with Acknowledged, Exempt or Refused buttons. Anyone still pending gets a reminder and their reminder count goes up.

After the round the policy owner gets one consolidated Chase outstanding acknowledgements task listing everyone outstanding, with a reminder and escalation to their manager if it sits. Staff have no app accounts, so every task goes to the person who installed and activated the package. Everything is built in.

packages.title: Policy attestation
packages.summary: A monthly campaign: employees confirm they have read the policies due for them, with reminders, escalation to compliance and an audit trail of attestations.
packages.description:
Policy attestation runs your read-and-understood campaigns. On the first of each month it reads the Policies data table, picks the active policies whose next due date has arrived and lists active employees from your HR system.

Each employee gets their own Attest policy run with only the policies for their department plus the ones for everyone. They tick "I have read and understood" and attest, or raise a question; questions go to the compliance officer, who answers (the attestation goes back to the employee) or marks them exempt. Reminders go out before the due date, open requests escalate to the compliance officer after 10 days, and every attested policy is written to the Attestations table with the version and date. The policies' next due dates roll forward by their frequency and the compliance officer gets a campaign summary.

Adapt the Policies rows (audience is a department name or "all"), the HR system reference to your API, the schedule, and the reminder and escalation timings on the attestation step.

Assignees: pick the default recipient for attestation tasks (used when an employee has no workspace user id; return workspace_user_id from the HR API, or map it, to send each task to the employee) and the compliance officer who answers questions and receives escalations.
Edit the Policies rows: version, document link, audience (a department name as the HR system spells it, or "all"), frequency in days and next due date.
Set compliance_email on the workflow to the inbox that receives the campaign summary, and change the schedule if your campaigns run on another day.
Email: configure EMAIL_PROVIDER on the instance so summaries and receipts are delivered (the steps continue on error).

packages.title: Risk register
packages.summary: Anyone raises a risk on a form; a 5×5 matrix rates it, the owner accepts, mitigates or escalates within an SLA, and a weekly job re-reviews due risks.
packages.description:
Risk register gives you a living register instead of a spreadsheet nobody opens. The Risks table holds each risk with its category, department, likelihood, impact, score, rating, owner, controls, response, mitigation plan, residual score and next review date. Six sample risks are included so the register is not empty on day one.

Anyone can raise a risk on the Raise a risk form page: a title, category, description, likelihood and impact (1-5 with plain-language labels), existing controls and the risk owner as a Person. The Risk submission workflow scores it (likelihood × impact), rates it with the Risk rating decision table (Low, Medium, High, Extreme), sets an SLA for the owner's review by rating and adds it to the register.

The owner reviews it in a task form with Accept, Mitigate and Escalate buttons: a mitigation plan, target date and residual rating are recorded, an escalation emails the risk committee, and the task escalates to the owner's manager if it sits for three days. A second workflow, Weekly risk review, runs every Monday: every open risk whose review date has passed goes back to its owner through a sub-workflow (still valid, rating changed, close risk). No integrations needed.

Set the risk committee address in the "Risk committee email" steps of Risk submission and Weekly risk review (risk-committee@example.com).
Tune the Risk rating decision table (thresholds, SLA days, review frequency) and the weekly schedule's day, time and time zone.

packages.title: Safety inspection checklist
packages.summary: Every month, a safety inspection checklist task for each site with Pass / Fail buttons; failures raise a corrective action and are logged.
packages.description:
Safety inspection checklist runs your monthly workplace inspections without paper forms. On the first of each month the workflow reads the Inspection sites table and starts a Site inspection sub-workflow for every site marked Inspect monthly.

Each inspection is a checklist task form: sixteen yes/no checks grouped under fire safety, housekeeping, equipment and first aid headings with dividers, in a compact two-column grid, plus findings and a photo link. Pass records the result; Fail counts the failed checks, records them in the Inspections table, flags the site, emails the site manager and raises a corrective action task due in a week, which can be completed or sent back for re-inspection.

The main run gives the health and safety lead a sign-off task for the round, so the committee gets one summary each month. Reminders and escalation to the manager keep inspections on time. Everything is built in.

packages.title: Supplier risk review
packages.summary: Adding a supplier or flagging it for review pulls a fresh risk rating, sets the tier and next review date, and sends high-risk suppliers to procurement.
packages.description:
Supplier risk review keeps your supplier register's risk ratings current. It runs whenever a row in the Suppliers data table is created, or updated with "Review requested" ticked, and fetches the supplier's financial score, cyber score, ESG flags and sanctions screening from your risk-intelligence provider.

The Supplier risk decision table combines those scores with the supplier's criticality and annual spend into a risk tier, a review cadence and a recommended action. The workflow writes the tier, scores and next review date back to the row and clears "Review requested", so its own update does not start another review. High and critical suppliers go to procurement as a User Task to accept the risk, agree a mitigation plan or plan an exit, with a five-day SLA; the business owner is told when the supplier is flagged and when it is decided.

Adapt the Supplier risk rules to your risk appetite, the reference to your provider's API, and the Suppliers columns to your register.

packages.title: Workplace incident log
packages.summary: A safety-themed incident form, severity and SLA from a decision table, an incident register with 7-year retention and an investigation task with Close / Escalate.
packages.description:
Workplace incident log gives everyone one simple place to report injuries, near misses, damage and environmental incidents. The Report a workplace incident form has a safety-orange theme and a grid layout; picking the site from the Incident sites table fills in the site manager.

Each report starts the Incident response workflow through its Form submitted trigger. The Incident severity decision table turns the incident type and worst injury into a severity, a response time in hours, whether a formal investigation is needed and whether the regulator may need to be told. The workflow sets an SLA, adds the incident to the Incidents register (with a 7-year review retention policy applied to the row) and emails the site manager.

When an investigation is needed, the health and safety lead gets an investigation task due within the SLA, with root cause, contributing factors and corrective actions, and Close or Escalate buttons. Escalations email the site manager and go to a senior review. Everything is built in.

packages.title: Asset register & check-out
packages.summary: A register of loanable equipment with a check-out form, a due-back return task with a reminder, and Returned / Damaged outcomes that update the register.
packages.description:
Asset register & check-out replaces the clipboard by the equipment cupboard. The Assets table is your register: tag, name, category, home location, serial number, condition, replacement value and whether each item is available, out or in repair. Sample rows cover loan laptops, AV kit, a camera, tools, a pool car and safety equipment.

People borrow from the Asset check-out form page. They search for the asset (only available items are offered) and its category, location and condition fill in by themselves; they pick the borrower as a Person, set the due-back date and accept responsibility. Check out shows a success screen.

The Form submitted trigger starts the workflow: it double-checks the asset is still available, marks it checked out in the register, logs the loan in the Check-outs table and emails the borrower a receipt. The borrower then gets a Return task due on the due-back date, with a reminder the day before. Returned puts the asset back in the register with its new condition; Damaged sends it for repair and records what went wrong. A two-year retention policy is included for the loan records. No integrations needed.

packages.title: Car-pool & fleet booking
packages.summary: Book a pool car on a themed form: service and clash checks, a decision table for long, multi-day or weekend trips, coordinator approval and a confirmation email.
packages.description:
Car-pool & fleet booking replaces the key cabinet sign-out sheet. People open the Pool car booking start form, pick a vehicle from the list (seats and EV are in the name), give the pick-up and return times, destination, rough distance and how many are travelling.

The workflow reads the vehicle from the Vehicles table and stops straight away if it is in service. It then looks for confirmed bookings in the Bookings table that overlap the requested times, and a clash is declined with the clashing booking reference. Otherwise the Booking approval decision table decides whether the fleet coordinator must approve: more people than seats, trips of 300 km or more, more than three days, or weekend use.

Standard bookings are confirmed at once. The others give the coordinator an Approve / Reject task with a reminder and escalation. Every booking is recorded, and the driver gets a confirmation with where the keys are and the fuel or charge card, or an email saying why it could not go ahead. Everything is built in.

packages.title: Event registration with session choices
packages.summary: A four-step registration page with an attendee table, first and second session choices, slider, rating and rich text; seats are checked by a decision table and waitlisted groups go to the organiser.
packages.description:
Event registration with session choices books groups into limited-seat sessions using only UserTasks features and the official form controls. The registration page has four steps with a progress bar and a review step: an event lookup that fills the date and venue from the Events table, a Table control for the attendees (name, email, dietary needs, accessibility needs), first and second choice sessions looked up in the Sessions table (only the sessions of the chosen event), a Slider for how many sessions they plan to attend, a heart Rating for interest in networking and a Rich text box for questions to the speakers.

The Event registration workflow counts the attendees with COUNT, reads the event and both sessions, and a Seat allocation decision table compares the spare seats with the size of the group: the first choice if it fits, else the second, else the waitlist. The registration is saved to the Registrations table, the seats taken go up on the session and the event, and a loop records every attendee in the Attendees table and emails each one their session; the person who registered gets a booking summary.

A waitlisted group becomes a task for the organiser (the person who installed the package) with a two-day SLA, a reminder and escalation: an Info card shows the group and both choices, a Progress bar how full the first choice is, and the organiser either offers another session (the group is then booked and emailed) or keeps them on the waitlist with a message.

The Organiser dashboard page shows a Progress bar of the chosen event's seats filled, Chart controls of seats taken against capacity per session and registrations by status from the data tables, Saved report controls for attendees by session and by dietary need (workflow variables), and a button that emails the event's attendee list with the catering numbers.
packages.start: Starts from a form page: share the Event registration with sessions page (/f/<id>) with staff or signed-in guests, or submit it from your own site through the forms API.

Replace the sample rows in Events and Sessions with your own (keep the Session column unique: it is what the session lookups store); delete the sample Registrations and Attendees rows when you go live.
Waitlisted groups go to the person who installed the package: change the Offer an alternative session step's assignee in the designer if someone else organises the events.
Edit the Seat allocation decision table to change how seats are given out.
Optional: apply the "Registrations: 12 months after the event" retention policy, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER so the confirmations are delivered (the console provider logs them).

packages.title: Meeting room booking
packages.summary: Book a room from a themed start form; rules send large, long or catered bookings to facilities for approval, everything else is confirmed straight away.
packages.description:
Meeting room booking gives people one simple, branded form to ask for a room: meeting title, room, date, start time, duration, number of attendees, catering and external guests. The Rooms table holds every bookable room with its floor, seats and equipment, so facilities can keep it up to date without touching the workflow.

The workflow reads the chosen room and checks the request against the Room booking approval decision table: more attendees than seats, a large room (12+ seats), a booking longer than four hours or catering all need facilities approval; anything else is confirmed automatically. Every request is recorded in the Room bookings table with the rule that applied.

Facilities get an approval task with Approve and Reject buttons, choose the room setup, tick that catering is ordered and leave a note for the organiser. The organiser gets a confirmation email with the room details, or the reason it could not be approved. No integrations needed.

Adjust the Room booking approval rules (seat threshold, maximum hours, catering) to your policy.
Optional: set EMAIL_PROVIDER so confirmations are delivered (the console provider logs them).

packages.title: Customer satisfaction (CSAT / NPS) survey
packages.summary: A three-step survey page with star rating, 0-10 NPS slider, Likert matrix and rich-text comment; a decision table classifies each answer and detractors get a follow-up call with an SLA.
packages.description:
Customer satisfaction (CSAT / NPS) survey is a complete feedback loop built only from UserTasks features and the official form controls. The survey page has three steps with a progress bar and a review step: a 1-5 star Rating, a 0-10 Slider for how likely the customer is to recommend you, a Likert matrix on speed, knowledge, ease and value (with N/A), and a Rich text comment.

Every answer starts the Survey response workflow. A decision table turns the scores into promoter, passive or detractor with NPS points (+100, 0, -100: their average is the NPS) and decides whether someone follows up and how fast. The response is saved in the Survey responses data table, which ships with six months of sample answers.

Detractors (and unhappy passives) become a follow-up task for the person who installed the package with a 24 or 48 hour SLA, reminders and escalation to their manager. The task shows the customer's answers on an Info card and records the root cause, a call rating, call notes and what was agreed, which is emailed to the customer. Everyone else gets a thank-you email.

The Survey results page is a small dashboard: a Chart of NPS by month and a doughnut of promoters, passives and detractors from the data table, the NPS by product area and the open follow-ups as Saved reports (workflow variables and task reports), and a button that emails a month's summary.

packages.title: Employee pulse survey
packages.summary: A stepped engagement survey with Likert sections, an eNPS slider and mood rating; scores and risk bands are worked out, and named at-risk answers get a manager follow-up with an action plan.
packages.description:
Employee pulse survey is a monthly engagement check built only from UserTasks features and the official form controls. The survey page has six steps with a progress bar and a review step: four Likert scale matrices (wellbeing, manager & team, growth, workload; agree / disagree with N/A), a 0-10 Slider for how likely the employee is to recommend working here (eNPS), a heart Rating for mood, the department, an "Answer anonymously" option and a Rich text box for one thing to change. The manager Person field only shows when the answer is not anonymous.

Every answer starts the Pulse response workflow. Set Variable expressions average each section (ignoring N/A) and turn all the answers into an engagement score out of 100; a decision table maps engagement, mood and eNPS to Thriving, Okay or At risk and decides whether a follow-up is needed. The answer is saved in the Pulse responses data table, without a name when anonymous; the table ships with 30 sample answers across six departments and three monthly rounds.

Named at-risk answers become a private follow-up task for the manager (or the person who installed the package when no manager was picked) with an SLA, a reminder and escalation. The task shows the scores on an Info card and a Progress bar, and records an action plan in a Table control (action, owner, due date) plus conversation notes, which are emailed to the employee. Anonymous at-risk answers never create a personal task: they are logged and counted in the HR aggregate.

The Pulse results page is a dashboard: Chart controls for average engagement by department, eNPS by round and the risk-band split from the data table, Saved report controls for section averages and open follow-ups, an Info card explaining the scores, and a button that emails a round summary.
packages.start: Starts from a form page: share the Employee pulse survey page (/f/<id>) with signed-in employees each month, or submit it from your own app through the forms API.

The Likert scale, Slider, Rating, Rich text, Progress, Info card, Table, Chart and Saved report controls install with the package (Extensibility → Form controls).
Follow-ups go to the manager the employee picks; without one they go to the person who installed the package (an HR partner, for example).
Edit the Engagement risk band decision table to change the thresholds or follow-up days; delete the sample rows in Pulse responses when you go live.
Optional: apply the "Pulse responses: 18 months" retention policy, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER so the thank-you, plan and summary emails are delivered (the console provider logs them).

packages.title: Site inspection with corrective actions
packages.summary: A four-step inspection page with a checklist table, star rating, photos and signature; a decision table sets the outcome band and every failed item becomes a signed-off corrective action.
packages.description:
Site inspection with corrective actions turns a safety walk-round into tracked, evidenced fixes using only UserTasks features and the official form controls. The Site safety inspection page has four numbered steps and a review step: a site lookup that fills the site manager, address and risk class from the Sites table; a Table control holding the checklist, pre-filled with eight standard items, where each row is marked Pass, Fail or N/A with an area, a severity and notes; a star Rating for the overall site condition, photo uploads and Rich text observations; and an Info card summary with the inspector's Signature.

The Site inspection workflow counts the failures with FILTER_WHERE and COUNT, works out the pass rate and the worst severity, and an outcome band decision table chooses Compliant, Minor actions, Major actions or Stop work with a close-out SLA in days. The inspection is saved to the Inspections table, the site's last result is updated, the site manager is emailed the report with the photos, and a Stop work result sends a stop-work alert straight away.

Every failed item is logged as an Open row in the Corrective actions table with a due date from a second decision table (high 2 days, medium 7, low 14), then becomes a corrective action task for the inspector with a reminder and manager escalation. The task shows the failed check on an Info card and a Progress bar of the actions closed so far, and records the fix, the root cause, photo evidence and a Signature sign-off; the site manager is emailed the evidence. When the last action is done the safety manager (the person who installed the package) gets a review task with an Info card summary, a Progress ring of the actions closed and a confidence Rating.

The Inspection overview page is the safety manager's dashboard: Chart controls of the open actions by severity and by site from the Corrective actions table, Saved report controls for failures by severity per site (workflow variables) and the open corrective action tasks, and a button that emails a digest of the open or overdue actions.
packages.start: Starts from a form page: inspectors open Forms → Site safety inspection (or its /f/ link on a phone or tablet) and submit it at the end of the walk-round.

setup: Nothing to configure: install it and open Forms → Site safety inspection (share its /f/ link with your inspectors) and Forms → Inspection overview.
The Table, Rating, Rich text, Info card, Signature, Progress, Chart and Saved report controls install with the package (Extensibility → Form controls).
Replace the sample rows in Sites with your own sites and site managers; delete the sample Inspections and Corrective actions rows when you go live.
Edit the checklist's starting rows on the form (the Checklist field's Starting rows) for your site types, and the two decision tables for the outcome bands and the days to fix.
Corrective actions go to the inspector who submitted the form and the review to the person who installed the package: change the assignees in the designer if your safety team works differently.
Optional: apply the "Inspections: 7 years" retention policy, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER so the report, stop-work and digest emails are delivered (the console provider logs them).

packages.title: Training feedback, quiz and certificate
packages.summary: Course feedback with ratings and a Likert matrix, a scored six-question quiz and a signed attestation; passes get a PDF certificate by email, near misses a retake task and fails a booked session.
packages.description:
Training feedback, quiz and certificate turns the end of a course into feedback, an assessment and a certificate, built only from UserTasks features and the official form controls. The Training feedback and quiz page has four numbered steps and a review step: the learner looks up the course in the Courses data table (title, trainer, pass mark and certificate validity fill in), rates the trainer and the content with the Rating control, answers a Likert scale matrix on course quality, takes a six-question multiple-choice quiz on information security basics and signs an attestation with the Signature control.

The Quiz submitted workflow scores the answers with Set Variable expressions, lists the topics to revise, and a decision table compares the score with the course pass mark: at or above it passes, up to 20 points below means a retake, further below means a session. Every result is saved in the Quiz results data table, which ships with sample results across four courses.

A pass gets a certificate number and an expiry date from the course validity; the certificate is written as HTML with a Text template, converted to PDF on the server (no external API), recorded in Quiz results and emailed to the learner as an attachment. A retake becomes a task for the learner with their score on a Progress bar (warning below 60 %, good from 80 %) and the topics on an Info card. A fail becomes a task for the training coordinator to book a session, with an SLA, reminder and escalation.

The Training results page is a dashboard: Chart controls for the average score by course and the pass / retake / fail split from Quiz results, Saved report controls for the pass rate and average scores and ratings by course (workflow variables) and the open retakes and sessions, and a button that emails a summary and reminds every learner whose certificate expires soon.
packages.start: Starts from a form page: share the Training feedback and quiz page (/f/<id>) with signed-in learners at the end of a course, or submit it from your LMS through the forms API.

changelog.notes: Uses the 1.1.0 form controls: they appear with the form, with no visible loading.

setup: Nothing to configure: install it and open Forms → Training feedback and quiz (share its /f/ link) and Forms → Training results.
The Rating, Likert scale, Signature, Progress, Info card, Chart and Saved report controls install with the package (Extensibility → Form controls).
Replace the sample rows in Courses with your catalogue (code, title, pass mark, certificate validity, trainer) and delete the sample rows in Quiz results when you go live.
The quiz questions are on the form and their correct answers are in the Correct answers step of the Quiz submitted workflow: change both together for your own topic.
Session bookings go to the person who installed the package (the training coordinator); retakes go to the learner. Edit the Quiz result band decision table to change the margins.
Optional: apply the "Quiz results: 7 years" retention policy, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER so certificates and reminders are delivered (the console provider logs them).

packages.title: FOIA / public records request: evidence redaction and release
packages.summary: Public records requests from a form to release: statutory SLA, evidence gathering, AI-assisted redaction of video, photos, audio and documents, legal approval and an exemptions log.
packages.description:
Public records requests (US FOIA and state public records acts, the NZ Official Information Act, the UK Freedom of Information Act or your own policy) start on a standalone form page: the requester gives their details, the records they want, the date range and how to receive them. The workflow gives the request a reference, looks up the response deadline in a configurable rules table, sets an SLA to match and emails an acknowledgement with the date.

A records officer attaches the responsive records: body-worn camera or CCTV video, photos, interview audio and documents. Redact Video blurs faces, licence plates and on-screen ID numbers and bleeps personal details it hears; Redact Image does the same for each photo; the interview is transcribed, bleeped and its transcript redacted; Redact Document finds personal information in the statement for review. Each item gets a proposed exemption in the Exemptions log.

A legal reviewer compares every original with its redacted copy (originals stay restricted to the request and are never released) and approves a full or partial release, denies it or sends it back. On release the document is redacted, the cover letter and exemption log become PDFs merged into a release package, and the requester gets the package by email or a download link. No-records, extension and denial letters are included, every step is written to an audit trail table, and a 7-year retention policy is applied. Redaction aids the reviewer; it does not replace them, and the deadline and exemption rows are examples to adapt with your counsel, not legal advice.
packages.start: Starts from a form page: share the Public records request form (/f/<id>) on your website; each submission starts the workflow.
setup: Google Gemini (media AI): paste your API key from aistudio.google.com. Redaction runs with your own key; to use another provider (OpenAI, Azure AI Vision, AWS) add that integration and choose it on the media steps.
Records release portal: set the base URL and token of the system that hosts download links (or remove the Create release link step and send attachments only).
Assignees: pick the records officer who gathers records and the legal reviewer who approves releases.

Review the Records request rules and Exemption codes tables with your counsel: the rows are examples (deadline counts, day types, extensions and exemption codes differ by statute and agency). They are not legal advice.

Apply the "Records requests: 7 years" retention policy to the Records requests, Exemptions log and Request activity tables to match your records schedule, and set EMAIL_PROVIDER so requesters receive their letters.
Background media steps need FFmpeg (Docker image or FFMPEG_PATH) and the media job scheduler (process-media) running, as for any long video.

steps.title: Gather records

steps.title: Automated redaction

steps.title: Audit and retention
steps.body: Every step is recorded in the Request activity table and the request row gets the 7-year retention policy.

packages.title: Identity document capture (KYC) with redaction for storage
packages.summary: Customers upload an ID photo and a selfie: the document is read, checked by rules, the number blacked out for storage, and a person compares the photos and decides.
packages.description:
Identity document capture starts from a form page where the customer enters their name and date of birth, picks the document type and uploads a photo of the ID and a selfie (the phone camera opens).

Analyze Image reads the printed fields (name, date of birth, document number, expiry, issuing region) and returns face boxes; the selfie is checked for exactly one face. There is no face recognition or face matching anywhere in this package: the automated checks only compare the text with the form (a Regex step for the number format, conditions for name and date of birth) and the ID document checks decision table turns them into a result and a flag for the reviewer.

Redact Image blacks out the ID number on a copy of the document for storage. The reviewer sees the extracted fields next to the form, opens the original photos (restricted to the review) and compares the selfie with the ID photo themselves, then verifies, asks for new documents or rejects. Only the masked fields and the redacted copy go into the Verified identities table, with a retention policy.

setup: Google Gemini (media AI): paste your Gemini API key. It reads the document text and finds face and text boxes; it never identifies or matches faces.
Assignees: pick the KYC reviewer.
Adjust the ID document checks and the Regex pattern to the documents you accept; set the "Verified identities: 5 years" retention policy to your record-keeping rule.
Original uploads stay as restricted form attachments: purge them on your schedule (form files retention) once the review is done.

packages.summary: Motor claims with damage photos: AI damage assessment, decision-table triage and SLA, adjuster review, letters, and photos with faces and plates blurred for repairers.
packages.description:
Insurance claim photo assessment starts from a claim form page where the claimant enters their policy, what happened and uploads photos of the damage (the camera opens on phones).

Analyze Image describes the damage and returns a structured assessment: severity, damaged parts, a rough cost range, whether the vehicle looks drivable and whether the photo matches the story. The Damage triage decision table turns that and the cover into a band (fast track, standard, specialist or coverage check), an estimate band, a decision SLA and whether an inspection is suggested. Every photo is also copied with faces and licence plates blurred, because repairers do not need them.

The adjuster reviews the claim with the AI assessment clearly marked as a hint, picks a repairer from the Approved repairers table and approves the repair, asks for an inspection or declines. Approval and decline letters are generated as PDFs and emailed, and the chosen repairer gets the job with the blurred photos only. The adjuster always decides.

packages.title: Meeting recording to minutes and action items
packages.summary: Upload a meeting recording: transcript with speakers, AI-drafted minutes the organiser checks, a task for each action owner and the minutes emailed with an SRT.
packages.description:
Meeting recording to minutes starts from a form page where the organiser uploads an audio or video recording with the meeting name, date, attendees and who should get the minutes, and confirms everyone agreed to being recorded.

Transcribe Audio / Video turns the recording into a transcript with speaker labels and timestamps and writes SRT, VTT and text files. The Minutes writer agent reads the transcript and drafts a summary, the decisions and up to three action items with the owner and due date mentioned in the meeting.

The organiser gets a task with the draft in a grid form: they correct the summary and decisions, pick the owner of each action from the workspace people (the agent only suggests names, it never assigns) and send. Each owner then gets their own task with the due date, the Action items table tracks them, and the minutes go out by email as a PDF with the SRT subtitle file attached.

packages.title: Support call QA and PII-safe archiving
packages.summary: Each finished call is transcribed, card numbers and IDs are bleeped and masked, an AI agent scores it on your QA rubric, and low scores go to a supervisor.
packages.description:
Support call QA and PII-safe archiving starts when your telephony or contact-centre platform posts a finished call to the workflow: the call id, a download URL for the recording, the agent and the queue.

Transcribe Audio / Video separates the agent and the customer. Redact Video, used on the audio, bleeps card numbers, social security numbers, dates of birth and other personal details from the recording at the times they were spoken, and Redact Document masks the same values in the transcript. The Call QA scorer agent only ever sees the masked transcript: it scores greeting, verification, understanding, resolution, tone and closing, gives the customer sentiment and writes coaching notes.

The QA thresholds decision table sends calls with a low score, a negative customer or an account change without verification to a supervisor, who listens to the redacted recording, sets the final score and records the coaching. Only the redacted recording and transcript are archived, with a two-year retention policy.
packages.start: Headless: your telephony platform calls the start API (or an inbound webhook) when a call recording is ready.
setup: Google Gemini (media AI): paste your Gemini API key (transcription with speakers and the speech used for bleeping).

Assignees: pick the QA supervisor.

Create an inbound webhook for the workflow (or call the start API) from your telephony platform with call_id, recording_url, agent_name, agent_email, queue and call_date. Recording URLs must be reachable from UserTasks (signed URLs work).
Tune the QA thresholds; apply the "Call QA archive: 2 years" retention policy to the archive table. FFmpeg is needed for the bleeping (Docker image or FFMPEG_PATH).

packages.title: User-generated media moderation
packages.summary: Uploads arrive by API: AI safety analysis of images and videos, threshold rules that auto-approve or reject clear cases, a moderator queue for the rest, and the uploader is told.
packages.description:
User-generated media moderation starts when your site or app posts an upload to the workflow: its id, a download URL, whether it is an image or a video, the uploader and the caption.

Analyze Image (or Analyze Video for clips) describes the upload and answers a structured moderation question: a risk score from 0 to 1, the top category (nudity, violence, hate, harassment, self-harm, drugs, weapons, spam), a possible child safety concern, whether people are visible and a one-sentence reason. The Moderation thresholds decision table auto-approves low risk, auto-rejects high risk and sends borderline items, self-harm and any child safety concern to a person.

Moderators get a task with the AI reason clearly marked as a triage aid and approve or reject with the guideline that applies. Your platform is called to publish or hide the upload (placeholder REST API), the uploader is emailed with how to appeal, and every decision is logged with a one-year retention policy.
packages.start: Headless: your platform calls the start API (or an inbound webhook) for each new upload.
setup: Google Gemini (media AI): paste your Gemini API key. (For image safety categories from a moderation endpoint, add an OpenAI or AWS integration and choose it on Analyze Image with the Safety feature.)
Content platform: set the base URL and token of the API that publishes and hides uploads, and adjust the Publish upload / Reject upload paths.
Assignees: pick the moderator (escalates to their manager after 8 hours).
Tune the Moderation thresholds to your guidelines. Route possible child safety issues to your legal reporting process: this package only queues them for a person.
Create an inbound webhook (or call the start API) from your platform for each upload; media URLs must be reachable from UserTasks.

packages.summary: An AI agent classifies each helpdesk ticket and drafts a reply; confident, low-risk answers go out automatically and the rest wait for a person.
packages.description:
AI ticket triage with human review puts an AI agent in front of your support queue without letting it answer everything on its own. Your helpdesk posts each new ticket (id, subject, body, customer email, channel and plan tier) to the workflow.

The Ticket triage agent returns the category, urgency, sentiment, a short summary, a suggested reply and its confidence. The Triage routing decision table then decides: confident how-to and low-urgency answers are posted automatically; security issues, critical tickets, enterprise billing and anything the agent is unsure about go to a person, with a queue and priority set either way.

The "Review AI triage" task shows the ticket, the summary and the draft reply. The reviewer corrects the category and priority, edits the reply and sends it, escalates the ticket (which moves it to the escalation queue and emails your support leads) or discards the draft and leaves the ticket for an agent. Every ticket is tagged so you can measure how often the AI reply was used. Adapt the agent instructions, the routing rules and the helpdesk calls to your tooling.
packages.start: Headless: your helpdesk posts each new ticket to the start API or an inbound webhook. People only see the tickets the rules send for review.
setup: AI model: set the base URL of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1 or your gateway) and its API key. Change the agent model if gpt-4o-mini is not available.
Helpdesk: set the base URL and API token of your helpdesk API. Post reply posts to /tickets/{id}/replies; Update ticket patches /tickets/{id}.
Assignee: pick the default support reviewer (runs can pass reviewer_id, e.g. per queue).
Tune the Triage routing rules: which categories and confidence levels may be answered automatically. Start strict and loosen as you review results.
Inbound webhook: create a webhook for the workflow and point your helpdesk's new-ticket trigger at it.
Email (optional): configure EMAIL_PROVIDER and set escalation_email for the escalation notice (the step continues on error).

packages.title: Document generation pipeline
packages.summary: Turn contract data from any app into a filled Word contract and Excel fee schedule, file both in your DMS and send the contract for e-signature.
packages.description:
Document generation pipeline produces contract documents without anyone opening Word. An application (your CRM, billing system or a back-office tool) posts the contract data: document type, customer, reference, start date, amount, term, signer and the URL of the Word template.

The Document templates table sets the title, file name pattern, DMS folder, retention period, body text and whether the document type needs a signature. The workflow fills the Word template's {{TITLE}}, {{CUSTOMER}}, {{DATE}}, {{AMOUNT}}, {{REFERENCE}} and {{BODY}} placeholders and, when an Excel template URL is passed, fills a fee schedule with the dates, total and monthly equivalent.

Both files are registered in your document management system with their metadata and retention. Document types that need a signature are sent to the signer through your e-signature service, and the signer gets an email with the signing link. Add rows for your own document types and point the two integrations at your DMS and e-signature provider.
packages.start: Headless: your application posts the contract data and template URL to the start API or an inbound webhook.
setup: Word template: put {{TITLE}}, {{CUSTOMER}}, {{DATE}}, {{AMOUNT}}, {{REFERENCE}} and {{BODY}} in your contract template and store it where the workflow can fetch it by URL (pass it as template_url).

Excel schedule (optional): a workbook whose first sheet takes labels in A2:A9 and values in B2:B9 (customer, reference, start and end date, term, total, monthly equivalent, document type), passed as schedule_template_url. Change the cells on Fill fee schedule to match your layout.
Document management system: set the base URL and API token. Register document posts the generated file URL and metadata to /documents.
E-signature service: set the base URL and API token. Create signature request posts to /signature-requests.
Edit the Document templates rows: titles, file name patterns, folders, retention days, body text and which types need a signature.
Email (optional): configure EMAIL_PROVIDER so signers get the signing email (the step continues on error).

packages.title: Event-driven ETL
packages.summary: Each new row in an Orders staging table is normalised, converted to the base currency, loaded into the warehouse and marked loaded or failed.
packages.description:
Event-driven ETL loads orders into your data warehouse the moment they are staged. Anything that writes a row into the Orders staging table (a CSV import, a form, another workflow or the API) starts a run for that row.

The workflow normalises the row: an upper-case currency code, a lower-case email, a trimmed customer name and an ISO order date. It looks up the exchange rate in the Currency rates table, converts the amount into the base currency, builds the warehouse record and posts it to the warehouse ingest API.

The staging row is then updated with load_status loaded (and the warehouse id) or failed (with the reason: no rate, or the HTTP status). The trigger listens to created events only, so these updates do not start new runs. Adapt the record fields to your warehouse schema and keep the rates current.

Adjust the Warehouse record step to your warehouse column names.
Load data by inserting rows into Orders staging with load_status pending.

packages.title: Order orchestration API
packages.summary: A synchronous order endpoint for your storefront: validate, price, fraud-screen, reserve stock, authorise payment and create the shipment in one call.
packages.description:
Order orchestration API turns one storefront call into a complete, ordered set of back-office steps. The storefront posts the order (order id, customer, email, lines with sku, quantity and price, the shipping address and a payment token reference from your payment provider) and waits for the answer: the workflow runs as middleware and its response is the result.

The workflow rejects incomplete orders straight away, then totals the lines and adds shipping and tax. The Fraud screening decision table looks at the order value, shipping country, whether the customer is new and whether billing and shipping countries differ, and returns accept, review or reject with a risk score. Accepted orders reserve stock in the inventory API, authorise the payment and create the shipment in the fulfilment API. If the payment is declined the reservation is released.

Orders flagged for review are still accepted, but the shipment is created on hold and a Manual fraud review runs in the background: a reviewer releases the shipment or cancels the order, voiding the authorisation and releasing the stock. The caller always gets result, order_status, reason, reservation_id, authorization_id, shipment_id and estimated_delivery. Card data never passes through the workflow.
packages.start: Headless and synchronous: the storefront posts each order to the workflow's middleware endpoint and receives the outcome in the HTTP response.
setup: Inventory API: set the base URL and token. Reserve stock posts to /reservations; Release reservation posts to /reservations/{id}/release.

Payments API: set the base URL and token of your payment provider or payment service. Authorise payment posts to /payments/authorize with the token reference; Void authorisation posts to /payments/authorizations/{id}/void.
Fulfilment API: set the base URL and token. Create shipment posts to /shipments; Update shipment patches /shipments/{id} to release or cancel a hold.
Assignee: pick the fraud reviewer who handles flagged orders (the Manual fraud review sub-workflow).
Edit the Fraud screening rules (home market, value thresholds) and the tax rate, shipping fee and free-shipping threshold variables.
Inbound webhook: create a middleware webhook for Order orchestration and point the storefront checkout at it. Keep the steps fast; the caller waits for the response.

packages.title: Scheduled data reconciliation
packages.summary: Every morning, yesterday's orders are matched to billing invoices; missing invoices and amount mismatches are recorded and a summary is sent.
packages.description:
Scheduled data reconciliation checks that every order was billed correctly. Each morning at 05:30 it reads yesterday's orders from your order system and the invoices for the same date from your billing API (or any date you pass as as_of).

For each order it finds the invoice with the same order id and classifies the pair: matched, missing invoice, or amount mismatch (a difference larger than the tolerance). Exceptions are inserted into the Reconciliation exceptions table with the amounts and difference, ready for finance to work through.

At the end it counts the results, emails a summary to finance operations and posts the same totals to an ops webhook. Adapt the two list endpoints, the matching key and the tolerance; nothing in the run needs a person.
packages.start: Runs every day at 05:30 UTC (change it on the Schedule trigger). Run it on demand with as_of to reconcile a past date.

Billing API integration: set the base URL and API token. List invoices by date calls GET /invoices?date=YYYY-MM-DD and reads data[] (invoice_number, order_id, amount).
Ops webhook integration: set the base URL (and token if needed) of the channel or monitoring webhook that receives the summary.
Set finance_ops_email and amount_tolerance on the workflow variables.
Email (optional): configure EMAIL_PROVIDER on the instance for the summary email (the step continues on error).

packages.title: Webhook multi-system sync
packages.summary: A CRM "account updated" webhook is validated and fanned out to the ERP, billing platform and support desk, with every result written to a sync log.
packages.description:
Webhook multi-system sync keeps customer master data consistent across systems without anyone touching it. Your CRM posts an "account updated" webhook with the account id, name, billing address, tax id, status, owner and change time.

The workflow rejects payloads without an account id or name, then builds a payload per target system and calls them one after another: PUT the customer into the ERP, POST a sync to the billing platform and PATCH the organisation in the support desk. An HTTP error from one system does not stop the others: each call is checked for a status of 400 or above and logged as a failure or a success in the Sync log table.

Adapt the three payloads to your systems' field names, point the integrations at your APIs and create an inbound webhook for the workflow in your CRM. The Sync log gives you a monitoring view and the rows you need to replay a failed sync.

Billing platform integration: set the base URL and API token. Sync billing account calls POST /accounts/{id}/sync.
Support desk integration: set the base URL and API token. Update support organisation calls PATCH /organizations/{id}.
Adjust the three "payload" steps to the field names each system expects.

Create an inbound webhook for the Account sync workflow (Settings → Webhooks) and register it in your CRM. Map the CRM field names to the workflow inputs in the webhook payload mapping if they differ.

controls.title: Address
controls.summary: Address search with suggestions from Google Places (key kept on the server) or a data table, saved as street, city, postcode, country and coordinates.
controls.description:
An address field that finds the address for people instead of making them type it in five boxes. As they type, suggestions come from the field's lookup source: Google Places API (New) through an integration that keeps the API key on the UserTasks server, another geocoding API, or a data table of your own sites. Choosing a suggestion stores a structured address (street, city, region, postcode, country and country code) with its coordinates and place id, ready for workflows, reports and the Map control.

It is a standard ARIA combobox: Up and Down move through the suggestions, Enter chooses, Escape closes, and screen readers hear how many addresses were found. If an address can't be found, "Enter the address manually" shows separate street, city, region, postcode and country inputs.

The package includes the Google Places integration (you enter your API key when installing), the text search API reference and a sample form that pairs Address with a Map. The Map control ships in the same package so the sample works on its own; it stays offline until an admin approves its tile host (tile.openstreetmap.org) in Extensibility → Form controls.

controls.readme:
# Address

`<ut-address>` — an address search field. Suggestions come from the field's **lookup source** (the
server calls it), and the chosen suggestion is stored as a structured address with coordinates.

## Value

Type `json`, or empty (`null`):

```json
{ "formatted": "1 Queen Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, New Zealand",
  "street": "1 Queen Street", "city": "Auckland", "region": "Auckland", "postcode": "1010",
  "country": "New Zealand", "country_code": "NZ", "lat": -36.8441486, "lng": 174.7671598,
  "place_id": "ChIJLWl7ckhIDW0RRhZBrhyJUBE" }
```

Parts are strings or `null`; `lat` / `lng` numbers or `null` (manual entry has no coordinates).
The schema requires `formatted` (1–500 characters) and bounds every part. Read-only views show
`{{value.formatted}}`.

Text typed but not chosen from the list makes the field invalid: "Choose an address from the list
(or enter it manually)".

Suggestions are parsed from:

- **Google Places API (New)**: `formattedAddress`, `addressComponents[] { longText, shortText, types }`,
  `location { latitude, longitude }`, `id`;
- **legacy Places / Geocoding**: `formatted_address`, `address_components[] { long_name, short_name, types }`,
  `geometry.location { lat, lng }`, `place_id`;
- **flat fields** (other providers, a data table of sites): `street`, `city`, `region`, `postcode`,
  `country`, `country_code`, `lat`, `lng` (and common synonyms such as `postal_code`, `state`, `latitude`).
  A named row (e.g. "Depot 7") shows its name with the address below.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Placeholder (`placeholder`) | text | Start typing an address | |
| Search after (`min_chars`) | number 1–20 | 3 | characters |
| Wait after typing (`debounce_ms`) | number 0–2000 | 350 | ms |
| Allow manual entry (`allow_manual`) | yes / no | yes | "Enter the address manually": street, city, region, postcode, country |
| Show address details (`show_details`) | yes / no | no | The parsed parts and coordinates under the field |
| Country hint (`country_hint`) | text | — | Appended to each search as ", New Zealand" |

## Keyboard and screen readers

An ARIA 1.2 combobox: the input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` (the
listbox) and `aria-activedescendant`; suggestions are `role="option"`. Down / Up move, Enter
chooses, Escape closes the list (a second Escape clears the text), Tab leaves. "N addresses found",
"No matches" and errors are announced in a polite live region; a spinner shows while searching. The
clear button is labelled "Clear the address".

## Capabilities

`lookup` only: `request('lookup', { query })` goes to the UserTasks server, which runs the field's
configured lookup source and returns the configured item fields. No network access from the
control.

## Security / setup

No Google API key ever reaches the browser. The form runs controls in a sandboxed frame with an
opaque origin and no referrer, so referrer-restricted browser keys cannot work, and an unrestricted
key in the page would be exposed. Instead the key lives in an integration on the server:

- **Integration** "Google Places API (New)": REST, `https://places.googleapis.com`, API key in the
  `X-Goog-Api-Key` header (you enter it when installing). Restrict the key to Places API (New).
- **API reference** "Places text search (addresses)": `POST /v1/places:searchText`, header
  `X-Goog-FieldMask: places.id,places.formattedAddress,places.addressComponents,places.location`,
  body `{"textQuery":"{{query}}","maxResultCount":5}`.
- **Field lookup**: source = that reference, `query` = `{{search}}`, results path `places`,
  display fields `formattedAddress`, `addressComponents`, `location`, value field `id`,
  min 3 characters, 400 ms debounce, 5 results, 300 s cache.
- **Sample form** "Address and location (sample)": Address plus a Map whose Location follows it.
- **Map control** (`ut-map`): the sample form uses it, so it is installed with this package. It needs network access to `tile.openstreetmap.org`; the install wizard lists that host, and the map stays blank until an admin approves it in **Extensibility → Form controls**.

Google bills Text Search per request; the cache and the minimum length keep the count down.
Check Google's terms for displaying and storing Places data.

Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

controls.readme:
# Chart

`<ut-chart>` — a bar, horizontal bar, line, area, pie or doughnut chart (Chart.js) of static data,
another field's rows, lookup results or a saved report. Follows the form theme in light and dark
mode, and is fully usable from the keyboard and with a screen reader.

## Value

Display only by default: the value stays empty (`null`). With **Selectable points** on, clicking a
point (or Enter on it) makes it the value:

```json
{ "label": "Mar", "value": 18, "series": "Sales" }
```

`label` (string) and `value` (number) are required; `series` is the dataset name, or `null` for a
single unnamed series. Read-only views show "Mar: 18".

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chart title (`chart_title`) | text | — | Heading and data-table caption (a report's name when empty) |
| Chart type (`chart_type`) | Bar / Horizontal bar / Line / Area / Pie / Doughnut | Bar | |
| Data source (`source`) | Static / Another field / Lookup / Saved report | Static | |
| Static data (`data`) | JSON | 4 sample months | `[{"label":"Jan","value":12}, …]` or `{"labels":[…],"datasets":[{"label":"Sales","data":[…]}]}` |
| Saved report (`report_id`) | text | — | For the Saved report source |
| Lookup query (`lookup_query`) | text | empty | Search text sent to the lookup |
| Label field (`label_field`) | text | first text field | Row field / report column for the labels |
| Value field (`value_field`) | text | first numeric field | |
| Series fields (`series_fields`) | list | — | Several numeric fields, one series each |
| Group by label (`aggregate`) | None / Sum / Count / Average | None | Groups rows with the same label |
| Show legend (`show_legend`) | yes / no | yes | Pie, doughnut and multi-series charts |
| Stack series (`stacked`) | yes / no | no | |
| Colours (`colors`) | list of #hex | theme primary + companions | |
| Chart height (`height`) | number 120–1000 | 280 | Pixels; the width follows the form |
| Selectable points (`selectable`) | yes / no | no | |

## Context

| Name | |
|---|---|
| `data` | For **Another field**: a field whose value is a list of rows (e.g. an editable table). |

## Data sources

- **Static** — the `data` property.
- **Another field** — rows from the `data` context field, with Label field / Value field / Series fields.
- **Lookup** — `request('lookup', { query })` against the field's lookup source (set Min characters
  to 0). Each item's `fields` (or `data`) give the columns; without them the item's label and
  numeric value are used.
- **Saved report** — `request('report')` runs the report chosen in `report_id` as the person filling
  in the form; the first text column is the label and the first numeric column the value unless set.

Loading shows a placeholder; a failed request shows the host's message inline (`role="alert"`).

## Keyboard and screen readers

The canvas is hidden from assistive technology. The plot is one Tab stop (a named group): Left /
Right move through the points (Up / Down for horizontal bars), Up / Down change series, Home / End
jump to the ends, Escape leaves the point. Each point is announced politely, e.g. "Mar: 18 (Sales),
3 of 5"; Enter selects it when points are selectable. **Show data table** renders every value in an
accessible table.

## Capabilities

`lookup` and `reports` (only used by those sources). No network access. Bundles Chart.js 4.5.1
(MIT, tree-shaken: bar, line, pie and doughnut controllers, category / linear scales, legend,
tooltip, filler), @kurkle/color 0.3.4 (MIT) and Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

# Info card

`<ut-info-card>` — an info, success, warning, error or neutral callout, or a key / value card, that
can show up to six other form values. Display only.

## Value

Value type `string`, but the control never sets it: the field stays empty and nothing is stored.
Read-only views (completed tasks, emails) show the card's title.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Variant (`variant`) | Info / Success / Warning / Error / Neutral | Info | Colour, icon and the screen-reader prefix |
| Title (`card_title`) | text | "Before you approve" | May use `{{field1}}` … `{{field6}}` |
| Text (`body`) | long text | sample sentence | Plain text, line breaks kept, `{{field1}}` … `{{field6}}` replaced |
| Layout (`layout`) | Callout / Key / value | Callout | Key / value lists the mapped fields with labels |
| Field labels (`labels`) | list | — | Labels of field 1 … 6 for the key / value layout |
| Value format (`format`) | Automatic / As stored | Automatic | Automatic formats numbers and ISO dates for the reader's locale, Yes / No for booleans |
| Show icon (`show_icon`) | yes / no | yes | |

## Context

`field1` … `field6` ("Field 1" …): another field whose value the card shows as `{{field1}}` … .
Lists are joined with commas; choice objects show their label.

## Keyboard and screen readers

Nothing to operate. The card is `role="note"` (warning and error cards are `role="status"`, a
polite live region, so a change is announced) named by its title. The variant is read first from a
visually hidden prefix ("Warning: Over budget for Marketing"); the icon is decorative. Placeholders
are filled as text: HTML in values or in the text is shown, never interpreted.

## Capabilities

None: no network, lookups or files. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause). The warning colour uses
`--ut-warning` when the theme provides it (the theme has no warning token yet; the fallback amber
passes contrast in light and dark mode).

controls.readme:
# Likert scale

`<ut-likert>` — a survey matrix: several statements rated on the same scale. A matrix with the
scale across the top on wide forms; one card per statement, with the labels spelled out, on phones.

## Value

An object with one entry per answered statement, or empty (`null`) when nothing is answered:

```json
{ "the_request_was_handled_quickly": 4, "the_staff_were_helpful_and_courteous": 5, "i_would_recommend_us_to_a_colleague": 0 }
```

- Keys are made from the statement text: lowercase, every run of other characters becomes `_`
  (duplicates get `_2`, `_3`, …). Renaming a statement changes its key.
- Values are the point on the scale, 1 = the first label (e.g. Strongly disagree), and 0 for N/A.
- The server checks it is an object of whole numbers from 0 to 10. Read-only views show the JSON.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Statements (`statements`) | list | three sample statements | One row each |
| Scale (`scale`) | Agree (5) / Agree (7) / Satisfaction (5) / Frequency (5) / Custom | Agree (5) | |
| Custom scale labels (`scale_labels`) | list | — | 2–10 labels, lowest first |
| Offer N/A (`show_na`) | yes / no | no | Stored as 0 |
| Every statement must be answered (`all_required`) | yes / no | no | "Answer every statement (2 left)" until done |

Scales: Strongly disagree · Disagree · Neutral · Agree · Strongly agree; the 7-point version adds
Somewhat disagree / Somewhat agree; Very dissatisfied … Very satisfied; Never · Rarely · Sometimes ·
Often · Always.

## Keyboard and screen readers

Each statement is a radio group labelled by the statement, with one Tab stop: Tab / Shift+Tab move
between statements, the arrow keys choose within a statement (like native radio buttons), Home /
End jump to the ends, Space or Enter chooses the focused point and Delete clears that statement.
Each option is announced by its label ("Agree"). Targets are at least 40 px tall.

## Capabilities

None: no network, lookups or files. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

controls.title: Map
controls.summary: Shows an address or coordinates from another field on an OpenStreetMap map, and can let people drop a pin to record a location.
controls.description:
A map for any form that deals with places: a site visit, a delivery drop-off, a fault report, an event venue. Map it to an Address field (or any field holding coordinates or "lat,lng" text) and it centres on that location with a pin, following the field as it changes.

Keyboard users Tab to the map, pan with the arrow keys, zoom with + and -, and press Enter to drop the pin at the centre (a crosshair marks it).

controls.readme:
# Map

`<ut-map>` — an OpenStreetMap map (Leaflet) that shows a location from another field and,
optionally, lets people drop a pin.

## Value

Type `json`: `{ "lat": number, "lng": number }` (latitude −90…90, longitude −180…180, six decimals),
or empty (`null`). With **Let people drop a pin** off the control never changes the value: it only
shows the mapped location. Read-only views (completed tasks, emails, mobile) show
`-36.844149, 174.76716`; on the form, read-only shows the map with the pin and no picking.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Map style (`tiles`) | OpenStreetMap, dimmed in dark mode / OpenStreetMap, always light | dimmed in dark mode | |
| Zoom (`zoom`) | number 1–19 | 15 | Zoom used when the map centres on a location |
| Map height (`height`) | number 160–800 | 320 | px |
| Let people drop a pin (`pick`) | yes / no | no | Click / tap / drag the pin / Enter / the coordinate inputs set the value |
| Show coordinates (`show_coordinates`) | yes / no | yes | Latitude and longitude under the map (always editable inputs in pick mode) |

## Context

| Name | What to map | |
|---|---|---|
| `location` | An Address field (`{ lat, lng, … }`), `{ latitude, longitude }`, `{ lat, lon }` or `"lat,lng"` text | When it changes the map centres on it and shows the pin. In pick mode the new location also becomes the value (people can then fine-tune it). |

## Keyboard and screen readers

The map is an `application` region named by the field label plus the pin's coordinates. Tab to it:
arrow keys pan, `+` / `-` zoom (Leaflet's keyboard handling). In pick mode a crosshair marks the
centre while the map has keyboard focus and Enter or Space drops the pin there. The Latitude and
Longitude inputs (a "Coordinates" group) set the pin exactly, Clear removes it, and changes are
announced in a live region. Zoom buttons are 32 px. Animations are off with
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Capabilities

`network`, host `tile.openstreetmap.org` (an administrator approves it in Extensibility → Form
controls). Public tile servers refuse requests without a Referer, and a sandboxed frame (opaque
origin) never sends one, so the map asks the host for each tile (`tile` request): the UserTasks server
fetches it from OpenStreetMap with an identifying User-Agent and Referer, caches it, rate-limits per
user, and serves it only when the host is approved for this control. The frame draws it through a
`blob:` URL that is revoked as soon as the image has decoded. Until the host is approved the map shows
a plain background, the pin and "Map tiles are blocked until an administrator approves … (Extensibility →
Form controls)". Attribution ("© OpenStreetMap contributors") is always visible.

Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause) and Leaflet 1.9.4 (BSD-2-Clause; its CSS is inlined in the shadow
root without the PNG images). The pin is an inline SVG.

## Notes

- OpenStreetMap's tile servers are a free, donation-funded service with a
  [usage policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/): fine for light form traffic;
  for heavy use fork the control for a commercial or self-hosted tile server (CARTO's free basemaps need a known referrer, which a sandboxed frame never sends).

controls.description:
Put the document people need to read right next to the questions about it: the contract to approve, the quote to check, the policy to acknowledge, the invoice to code. Map an Attachments field in the designer and the viewer shows its first PDF, or allow uploads so people can choose a PDF themselves; the uploaded file becomes the field's value.

Pages render one at a time, sharp on high-density screens, with previous and next page, zoom in and out, fit to width and rotate. The viewer is keyboard friendly (Page Up and Page Down turn pages, + and - zoom, Home and End jump to the first and last page) and each page is announced as "Page 2 of 7, contract.pdf" followed by the page's text, so screen-reader users can read the document too.

PDF.js runs entirely inside the form's sandbox: no worker, no network access and no script evaluation, and the file is read through the form's own file service, which only hands over files that belong to the form. Password-protected, damaged and non-PDF files show a clear message instead of a broken page.

controls.readme:
# PDF viewer

`<ut-pdf-viewer>` — shows a PDF inside the form (a contract, a quote, a policy, an invoice), from
an Attachments field the designer maps or from an upload, one page at a time with zoom, fit to
width and rotation. Each page's text is available to screen readers.

## Value

Type `files`: `[{ "id", "name", "size", "type" }]` (at most one file), or empty (`null`).
The value is only set when uploads are allowed and the person uploads a PDF; a document shown
from the mapped Attachments field is not copied into this field. Read-only views (completed
tasks, mobile, emails) list the uploaded file's name.

Which PDF is shown:

1. the control's own value (an uploaded PDF), if there is one;
2. otherwise the first PDF (by type `application/pdf`, or a `.pdf` name) in the `document`
   context entry;
3. otherwise an empty state: "No document yet — map an Attachments field in the designer, or
   allow uploads".

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Allow uploading a PDF (`allow_upload`) | yes / no | no | Shows "Choose a PDF"; the upload becomes the value (Replace / Remove once set). Up to 25 MB; the file must start with a PDF header |

## Context

| Name | | |
|---|---|---|
| `document` | Document | An Attachments field of the form; the first PDF in it is shown |

## Keyboard and screen readers

- The toolbar has Previous page / Next page, "Page 2 of 7" (announced politely when it changes),
  Zoom out / Zoom in, Fit to width (a toggle) and Rotate clockwise.
- The page area is a focusable region named "<label>: <file name>". In it: Page Down / Page Up
  turn pages (on a zoomed page they scroll first, then turn), Home / End go to the first / last
  page, Left / Right turn pages when the page isn't scrolled sideways, + / - zoom, 0 fits the width.
- The page canvas is an image named "Page 2 of 7, contract.pdf", followed by the page's text
  (from `page.getTextContent()`) in a visually hidden element. Scanned pages without a text layer
  say so.
- Loading is announced (`role="status"`); errors (not a PDF, damaged, password-protected, the
  request refused) are shown inline with `role="alert"`.

## Capabilities

`files`:

- `request('file', { id })` reads the bytes of the mapped Attachments field's PDF (the host only
  hands over files that are in the control's own value or its context values);
- `request('upload', { name, type, bytes })` stores an uploaded PDF (when uploads are allowed).

No network access. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause) and PDF.js (`pdfjs-dist` 5.4.624,
Apache-2.0), including its worker code. The module is about 1.4 MB.

## Security and sandbox notes

The form's sandbox forbids Workers and `eval`, so PDF.js runs its worker code in the main thread
(the "fake worker": the bundled `pdf.worker.min.mjs` is exposed as `globalThis.pdfjsWorker`) and
documents are opened with `isEvalSupported: false`, no URLs (`data` only, no range or stream
requests) and no `standardFontDataUrl` / `cMapUrl` / `wasmUrl`. Consequences: fonts a PDF doesn't
embed use the system's fonts (`useSystemFonts`), some CJK text in PDFs relying on external CMaps
may not render, and JPEG 2000 images (which need PDF.js's WebAssembly decoder) may be missing.
Only the current page is rendered (canvas capped at about 16 million pixels) to keep memory low.
Annotations, forms and links inside the PDF are not interactive.

Map the Current and Total context entries to fields of the form (numbers, a step name, or a list whose length counts), or type fixed values.

Set Warn below and Good from to turn the progress red with Needs attention or green with On track, so colour is never the only signal.
