# Progress

`<ut-progress>` — progress as a bar, a ring or named steps, from two mapped fields or fixed values.
Display only.

## Value

Value type `number`, but the control never sets it: the field stays empty (`null`) and nothing is
stored. Read-only views show the same progress.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Style (`appearance`) | Bar / Ring / Steps | Bar | |
| Current (`current_value`) | number | — | When the Current context entry is not mapped |
| Total (`total_value`) | number | 100 | When Total is not mapped; Steps uses the number of step names |
| Step names (`steps`) | list | — | For Steps, in order |
| Unit (`unit`) | text | — | e.g. tasks, hours |
| Show percentage (`show_percentage`) | yes / no | yes | |
| Label (`label_template`) | text | `{{current}} of {{total}} {{unit}}` | Also `{{percent}}`, `{{remaining}}`, `{{step}}`; plain text |
| Warn below (`warn_below`) | number 0–100 (%) | — | Error colour + "Needs attention" |
| Good from (`good_above`) | number 0–100 (%) | — | Success colour + "On track" |

## Context

| Name | |
|---|---|
| `current` | Progress so far: a number, a step number (1 = first) or a step name, or a list (its length counts) |
| `total` | The total or target: a number or a list (its length counts) |

Mapped context values win over the Current / Total properties.

## Keyboard and screen readers

Nothing to operate. Bar and ring are `role="progressbar"` named by the field label, with
`aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` / `aria-valuenow` and the label, percentage and status as
`aria-valuetext` ("7 of 12 tasks, 58.3%"). Steps is an ordered list with `aria-current="step"` on
the current step and the heading "Step 2 of 5: Review"; on narrow screens the steps stack
vertically. The threshold colours always come with text.

## Capabilities

None: no network, lookups or files. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

# Rating

`<ut-rating>` — a 1 to N rating with stars, hearts or circles, for satisfaction scores, priority
and quality checks. One Tab stop; the arrow keys change the rating like any radio group.

## Value

A whole number from 1 to the number of symbols, or empty (`null`) when nothing is chosen.
Required fields refuse an empty rating; the server checks the value is a whole number from 1 to 10.
Read-only views (completed tasks, mobile, submissions) show "4 of 5".

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Number of symbols (`max`) | number 2–10 | 5 | |
| Symbol (`symbol`) | Stars / Hearts / Circles | Stars | |
| Size (`size`) | Small / Medium / Large | Medium | 24 / 32 / 40 px |

A radio group named by the field label. Left / Right (or Up / Down) change the rating, Home / End
jump to the lowest / highest, Delete or Backspace clears it. Each symbol is announced as
"4 of 5: Very good".

## Capabilities

None: no network, lookups or files. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

controls.summary: A rich-text editor with bold, italic, underline, headings, lists, quotes and links, a character counter and strict sanitising of everything pasted in.
controls.description:
A compact editor for the long answers that plain text boxes make hard to read: incident descriptions, change summaries, meeting notes, customer replies. People can use bold, italic and underline, two heading levels, bulleted and numbered lists, quotes and links, and paste from documents, email or web pages without dragging the source's styling along.

Everything that reaches the editor or the stored value is rebuilt from a short allowlist of tags (paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, links, bold, italic, underline) with every attribute removed; links keep only https, http and mailto addresses and always open in a new tab. Scripts, images, frames, styles and event handlers never get through. The value stores the clean HTML together with a plain-text copy, so workflows, emails and search can use the text directly.

The toolbar is a proper ARIA toolbar with a single Tab stop and arrow-key navigation, every toggle announces whether it is on, and the usual shortcuts work (Ctrl/Cmd+B, I, U, K, Z). A counter shows the length against the limit and warns screen-reader users politely as they approach it.

changelog.notes: Workflow output: the field is now text — sanitised HTML by default, or plain text (Workflow output in the field properties) — with the plain text as <key>_text and the full { html, text } value as <key>_raw. Opens with no visible loading.
Fast typing no longer loses text: a late echo of an earlier keystroke from the form is recognised and ignored instead of re-rendering the editor.

controls.readme:
# Rich text

`<ut-rich-text>` — a compact rich-text editor: bold, italic, underline, two heading levels,
bulleted and numbered lists, quotes, links, clear formatting and undo / redo, with a character
counter. Everything typed, pasted, dropped or loaded is sanitised against a strict allowlist.

## Value

JSON `{ "html": string, "text": string }`, or empty (`null`) when the editor holds no text.

- `html` — sanitised HTML using only `p`, `br`, `strong`, `em`, `u`, `h2`, `h3`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`,
  `blockquote` and `a`. No attributes except on links: `href` (https, http or mailto only),
  `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and `target="_blank"`.
- `text` — the plain text with line breaks (list items start with `• ` or `1. `).

The server checks the shape (an object with the two strings, each at most 100,000 characters).
The control reports itself invalid when the text is longer than the maximum length ("Shorten the
text to 5000 characters") or the HTML exceeds 100,000 characters.
Read-only views (completed tasks, mobile, emails) show the plain text (`{{value.text}}`); the
control itself, when read-only, renders the sanitised HTML without an editor.

## Workflow output (1.1.0)

Workflows get text, not the object: `{{form.<key>}}` is the sanitised HTML (sanitised again by
the server) — or the plain text, when the form author sets **Workflow output: Plain text** in the
field's properties. `{{form.<key>_text}}` is always the plain text and `{{form.<key>_raw}}` the
whole `{ html, text }` value. Paths written for 1.0 (`{{form.<key>.text}}`) keep working.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Placeholder (`placeholder`) | text | — | Shown in the empty editor |
| Maximum characters (`max_length`) | number 1–100,000 | 5000 | Counted on the plain text; a counter shows "123 / 5000" |
| Toolbar (`toolbar`) | Full / Basic | Full | Basic: bold, italic, underline, lists, link, undo, redo |
| Minimum height (`min_height`) | number 60–1200 | 160 | Editor height in px before it grows |

## Keyboard and screen readers

The editor is a multi-line textbox (`role="textbox"`, `aria-multiline`) named by the field label
and described by its help text. The formatting toolbar (`role="toolbar"`) is one Tab stop:
Left / Right move between buttons, Home / End jump to the ends, Enter or Space applies. Toggle
buttons (bold, headings, lists, quote, link) expose `aria-pressed` for the formatting at the caret.

Shortcuts in the text: Ctrl/Cmd+B, I, U (bold, italic, underline), Ctrl/Cmd+K (link: an inline
box opens; Enter applies, Escape cancels; addresses without a scheme get https://, email addresses
get mailto:), Ctrl/Cmd+Z (undo), Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl/Cmd+Y (redo).
Near the limit the remaining characters are announced politely (`aria-live`).

Formatting uses the browser's editing commands (`document.execCommand`), feature-detected: where
they are unavailable the toolbar is hidden and the text still edits.

## Security

The sanitiser rebuilds content from scratch (DOMParser into an inert document, then new elements
via `createElement`); it never assigns untrusted HTML with `innerHTML`. Dropped elements keep their
text, except script, style, SVG, frames and similar, which are removed entirely. Pastes and drops
are intercepted and sanitised before insertion; the stored value is sanitised again on every change.

**Consumers must still sanitise `html` before rendering it anywhere else** (an email template,
another application): the UserTasks server validates only the value's shape and size, so a value
written through the API may contain anything. Where formatting isn't needed, use `text`.

## Capabilities

None: no network, lookups or files. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

controls.title: Saved report
controls.summary: Show a saved report inside a form as a sortable, paginated table or chart, with the permissions of the person filling it in. Optionally pick a row.
controls.description:
Bring the numbers someone needs into the form where they make the decision: open invoices on a payment approval, a customer's recent orders on a refund request, this month's incidents on a weekly review. Choose any saved report from Reports and the control runs it with the permissions of the person filling in the form, so people only ever see what they could already see in Reports: their own or shared reports, with their row-level rules.

The table sorts by any column, pages through the rows ("Rows 11-20 of 57"), formats numbers and dates for the reader's locale and scrolls sideways inside its own frame on a phone. # Saved report

`<ut-saved-report>` — shows a saved report from Reports inside a form, as a sortable, paginated
table or as the report's chart. The report runs with the permissions of the person filling in the
form: they see only their own or shared reports, with their row-level rules.

## Value

Empty (`null`) unless **Selectable rows** is on; then picking a row makes that row the value, an
object of the report's columns:

```json
{ "invoice": "INV-1042", "customer": "Kiwi Foods", "status": "Paid", "amount": 1088.5, "due": "2026-11-03" }
```

Picking the same row again clears it. The server checks the value is an object. Read-only views
show the row as JSON.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Saved report (`report_id`) | text, required | — | The report's id (from the address bar in Reports) |
| View (`view`) | Automatic / Table / Chart | Automatic | Automatic = the report's chart (bar, line, area, pie, horizontal or stacked bar), else a table |
| Rows per page (`page_size`) | number 1–200 | 10 | |
| Maximum rows (`max_rows`) | number 1–1000 | 100 | A note shows "Showing first 100 of 2,345 rows" when there are more |
| Chart height (`height`) | number 120–1000 | 280 | Pixels |
| Show the report's name (`show_title`) | yes / no | yes | Name and description above the table |
| Selectable rows (`selectable`) | yes / no | no | |

## Keyboard and screen readers

A real `<table>` with a caption (the report's name and current sort). Each column header is a
button: Enter or Space sorts ascending, again descending, announced through `aria-sort`. Previous /
Next page through the rows ("Rows 11-20 of 57"). With selectable rows each row starts with a toggle
button ("Select INV-1042", `aria-pressed`); clicking anywhere on the row also picks it. The chart
view has a text alternative listing the values and a Table switch. Loading sets `aria-busy`;
sorting, paging and selection are announced politely; errors from the host (for example "The
report is not shared with you") are shown inline as an alert. On a phone the table scrolls
sideways inside its own frame.

## Capabilities

`reports`: `request('report', { limit })` returns the report the designer chose. The control
cannot choose another report — the server reads `report_id` from the stored form and runs it as
the current user. No network access. Bundles Chart.js 4.5.1 (MIT, tree-shaken), @kurkle/color
0.3.4 (MIT) and Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

People sign with a finger on a phone, a pen on a tablet or a mouse on a desktop, undo a stroke or clear the pad, then press "Use this signature". The signature is trimmed to its ink, saved as a PNG through the same storage as the Attachments field, and the field keeps a reference to that file.

Keyboard and screen reader users can choose "Type your name instead": the name is drawn in a handwriting font and saved the same way. Completed tasks, emails and the mobile app show the signature file; the form shows the image with a "Signed" badge and, while the task is open, a "Sign again" button.

controls.readme:
# Signature

`<ut-signature>` — a signature pad. People sign with a finger, pen or mouse (or type their name),
press **Use this signature**, and a trimmed PNG is saved with the form's attachments.

## Value

Type `files`: an array with one stored file, `[{ "id", "name", "size", "type" }]`
(`signature.png`, `image/png`), or empty (`null`) before signing. The schema allows at most one
item. Read-only views (completed tasks, emails, mobile) list the file name; the form shows the
image with a "Signed" badge.

The upload happens when the person presses **Use this signature**, presses Enter in the typed
name, or leaves the control with ink on the pad. **Sign again** clears the value and shows an
empty pad.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ink colour (`pen_color`) | colour | dark ink on white; the theme's text colour on transparent | |
| Background (`background`) | White / Transparent | White | The saved PNG's background. Transparent images with light ink (dark mode) are hard to see on white paper |
| Pad height (`height`) | number 100–480 | 180 | px |
| Allow a typed signature (`allow_typed`) | yes / no | yes | "Type your name instead": drawn in a handwriting font |
| Prompt (`prompt`) | text | Sign above | Under the signing line |

## Keyboard and screen readers

The control is a group named by the field label. The drawing area is an image (`role="img"`)
whose name says whether ink is present. Keyboard users choose **Type your name instead**, type and
press Enter. Undo, Clear, Use this signature and Sign again are ordinary buttons; upload errors
are announced (`role="alert"`). The canvas sets `touch-action: none` so drawing never scrolls the
page, scales for the device pixel ratio and keeps the strokes when the width changes.

## Capabilities

`files`: uploads the PNG with `request('upload')` (the host's Attachments pipeline and its limits)
and reads a stored signature back with `request('file')` to show it (only the control's own value).
No network access.

Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause) and signature_pad 5.1.4 (MIT).

controls.summary: A range slider for numbers with a value bubble, mark labels such as Low, Medium and High, a unit or currency prefix and an optional exact-entry box.
controls.description:
A slider for any number that sits on a scale: a confidence or risk score from 0 to 100, a budget from $0 to $5,000, a discount percentage, a priority from 1 to 10. Set the minimum, maximum and step, add a prefix ($) or suffix (%, kg), and spread labels such as Low, Medium and High under the track. A small number box beside the slider lets people type an exact value when dragging is too coarse.

It is a native range input underneath, so keyboards and screen readers work as people expect: the arrow keys move one step, Page Up and Page Down move further, Home and End jump to the ends, and the value is announced with its unit and mark ("100%, High"). The thumb and track are large enough for touch.

A starting position can be shown without storing it: the field stays empty (and a Required field stays unanswered) until the person moves the slider or presses Enter to accept the start, so you can tell a deliberate answer from an untouched default.

changelog.notes: Dynamic properties: min, max can be bound to an expression, a data table or an API reference in the form designer (the host resolves them; no network capability needed).
Declares its workflow output: a number.

uses: Confidence or risk score from 0 to 100 on an assessment
Budget or spend limit from $0 to $5,000 on a request form
Discount or completion percentage on an approval step

# Slider

`<ut-slider>` — a range slider for numbers on a scale (scores, budgets, percentages), with a
value bubble, mark labels, a prefix or unit, and an optional number box for exact entry.
It is a styled native `<input type="range">`, so keyboard and screen-reader support are the
browser's own.

## Value

A number, or empty (`null`) until the person moves the slider. When a starting position is set,
the slider shows it with a dashed thumb and "not set" in the bubble, but nothing is stored until
the person moves the slider (or presses Enter / Space to accept the start) — so a Required field
can tell a deliberate answer from an untouched default.

The control reports itself invalid when the value is outside the minimum / maximum or not on a
step ("Choose a value from 0 to 100"). The server checks the value is a number.
Read-only views (completed tasks, mobile, submissions) show the number (`{{value}}`; the prefix
and suffix are not part of the stored value).

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum (`min`) | number | 0 | |
| Maximum (`max`) | number | 100 | |
| Step (`step`) | number > 0 | 1 | 1, 5, 0.5, … |
| Prefix (`value_prefix`) | text | — | Shown before the value, e.g. `$` |
| Suffix (`value_suffix`) | text | — | Shown after the value, e.g. `%` or ` kg` |
| Show value bubble (`show_value`) | yes / no | yes | A bubble above the thumb with the formatted value |
| Mark labels (`marks`) | list | — | Spread evenly under the track, lowest first: Low, Medium, High. Without marks the minimum and maximum are shown |
| Show number box (`show_input`) | yes / no | no | Type an exact value beside the slider |
| Starting position (`default_value`) | number | minimum | Shown, not stored, until the person moves the slider |

(The prefix / suffix props are not called `prefix` / `suffix` because `prefix` is a built-in
read-only property of DOM elements.)

## Keyboard and screen readers

A native slider named by the field label. Left / Right (or Up / Down) move one step, Page Up /
Page Down move further, Home / End jump to the minimum / maximum; Enter or Space accepts the
starting position while the field is empty. The value is announced with its prefix, suffix and
mark ("100%, High"; "Not set, starts at 50%" while empty). The number box is labelled
"<label>, exact value". The thumb is 24 px and the touch area 32 px tall.

## Capabilities

None: no network, lookups or files. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

controls.title: Table
controls.summary: An editable table for line items, attendees or readings, with typed columns, per-cell validation, totals and spreadsheet-style keyboard editing.
controls.description:
Collect repeating rows in one field: the line items of a purchase request, the attendees of an event, the readings of an inspection, the expenses of a trip. You define the columns (text, number, currency, date, choice from a list, or tick box), mark the required ones, set number bounds and widths, and choose whether people can add and delete rows, with a minimum and maximum row count.

Every cell is checked as people type: a required item left blank or a quantity below its minimum is marked on the cell itself and summarised for the form ("Row 2: Quantity must be at least 1"). An optional totals row sums the number and currency columns. Starting rows can be shown without being stored, so a template row never ends up in the submission by accident.

It works like a small spreadsheet from the keyboard: one Tab stop, arrow keys between cells, typing or Enter to edit, Enter to save and move down, Escape to cancel, Ctrl+Enter to add a row. Screen readers hear each cell with its column and row. On a phone the table scrolls sideways inside its own frame. The value is a list of plain objects with real numbers, booleans and ISO dates, ready for workflows and reports.

changelog.notes: Dynamic properties: default_rows can be bound to an expression, a data table or an API reference in the form designer (the host resolves them; no network capability needed).
Declares its workflow output: a list of rows (unchanged).

uses: Line items on a purchase request, with quantities, prices and a total
Attendee list for an event or training booking
Readings or defects recorded during an inspection
setup: Install the package: the control appears in Extensibility → Form controls and in the form designer's palette under Custom.
Drag Table onto a form and define the columns in the properties panel (key, label, type, required, options, min / max, width).
Set the row limits, whether people can add or delete rows, the currency for currency columns, and (optionally) the starting rows and the totals row.
controls.readme:
# Table

`<ut-table>` — an editable table with typed columns, per-cell validation, an optional totals row
and spreadsheet-style keyboard editing (an ARIA grid). For line items, attendees, readings,
expenses: anything that repeats.

## Value

An array of row objects keyed by column key, or empty (`null`) until the person edits the table.
Every row carries every column key:

| Column type | Stored as | Blank |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | `null` |
| `number`, `currency` | number (`1250.5`) — text that isn't a number is kept as typed and reported invalid | `null` |
| `date` | `"YYYY-MM-DD"` | `null` |
| `select` | the option text | `null` |
| `checkbox` | `true` / `false` | `false` |

```json
[{ "item": "Laptop", "quantity": 2, "unit_price": 1499 }]
```

The server checks the value is an array of objects with at most 200 rows. The control checks
each cell (required, number bounds, date format, select options) and the row count, marks bad
cells (`aria-invalid`, with the message under the value) and reports the first problem to the
form: "Row 2: Quantity must be at least 1 (and 2 more problems)". Cell errors show on rows
that have content, and on every row once the form marks the field invalid.
Read-only views (completed tasks, mobile, emails) show the value as JSON; the control itself,
when read-only, renders a plain table with formatted values and the totals.

## Properties

| Property | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Columns (`columns`) | JSON list | Item (text, required), Quantity (number, min 1), Unit price (currency, min 0) | `{ "key", "label", "type", "required", "options", "min", "max", "width" }`; up to 20 |
| Minimum rows (`min_rows`) | number 0–200 | 0 | Blank rows shown at the start; rows can't be deleted below it |
| Maximum rows (`max_rows`) | number 1–200 | 50 | |
| Allow adding rows (`allow_add`) | yes / no | yes | |
| Allow deleting rows (`allow_delete`) | yes / no | yes | |
| Show totals (`show_totals`) | yes / no | no | Footer row summing number and currency columns |
| Currency (`currency`) | text | USD | ISO 4217 code for currency columns |
| Starting rows (`default_rows`) | JSON list | — | Shown while the value is empty; stored only once the person edits |

## Keyboard and screen readers

The table is an ARIA grid named by the field label, with one Tab stop (roving focus):

- Arrow keys move between cells; Home / End go to the start / end of the row, Ctrl+Home /
  Ctrl+End to the first / last cell; Page Up / Page Down move five rows.
- Enter, F2, Space or simply typing starts editing a cell (typing replaces its content). In the
  editor, Enter saves and moves down (Shift+Enter up), Tab / Shift+Tab save and move to the
  next / previous cell, Escape cancels. Dates use the browser's date input, choices a native select.
- Delete or Backspace clears a cell; Space or Enter toggles a tick box.
- Tab / Shift+Tab move cell by cell and leave the table after the last / before the first cell.
- Ctrl+Enter adds a row (or use the Add row button). The last cell of each row is a "Delete row 2"
  button. Adding and deleting rows is announced politely.

Column headers and row numbers are real header cells, so every cell is announced with its column
and row; editors are labelled "Quantity, row 2". Errors are linked with `aria-describedby`.
On narrow screens the table scrolls sideways inside its own frame (the page doesn't).

## Capabilities

None: no network, lookups or files. Bundles Lit 3.3.3 (BSD-3-Clause).

actions.title: Crypto & IDs
actions.summary: UUID v4/v7 and ULIDs, SHA hashes, HMAC webhook signatures with a stored secret, base64/hex/URL encoding, random and one-time codes, and HS256 JWTs.
actions.description:
Crypto & IDs gives workflows identifiers and cryptography from the server's secure random generator. Generate random UUID v4s or time-ordered UUID v7s and ULIDs that sort by creation time, unbiased random codes from alphabets without look-alike characters (grouped like ABCD-EFGH), and numeric one-time codes with an expiry time and a hash to store instead of the code. Hash text with SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-384 or SHA-1 and encode or decode base64, base64url, hex and URL percent-encoding.

For integrations, HMAC signs a message with a key that an administrator stores once (hmac_key): the host computes the signature, so the key never reaches workflow builders or the action's code, and a received webhook signature is compared in constant time. Sign token and Verify token issue and check compact HS256 JSON Web Tokens with token_secret: expiry, not-before, issuer and audience are enforced, and invalid tokens come back with a reason instead of failing the workflow.
uses: Verify the HMAC signature of an incoming webhook before processing it
Issue a signed, expiring link token for an external approver and check it when they respond
Generate voucher or reference codes and time-ordered IDs for new records
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
For HMAC: in Extensibility → Workflow actions, open Crypto & IDs and set the hmac_key secret (e.g. your webhook provider's signing secret). For tokens: set token_secret to a long random value.
Drag Crypto & IDs onto a workflow and choose the function. For webhooks, map Message to the raw request body and Signature to check to the signature header, then branch on {{prefix_matches}}.
Try the included "Signed approval link (sample)" workflow from the API or its start form after setting token_secret: it signs a token for an approver, verifies it and hashes the request reference.
actions.readme:
# Crypto & IDs (`ut_crypto`)

Identifiers and cryptography for UserTasks workflows: UUID v4 and v7, ULIDs, SHA hashes, HMAC signatures with a stored secret, base64 / hex / URL encoding, random codes, one-time codes and compact HS256 JSON Web Tokens.

Official UserTasks workflow action, version 1.0.0. Source: `src/action.ts`; built module: `dist/action.js` (one self-contained ES module that runs in the UserTasks QuickJS sandbox).

## Operations

### UUID (`uuid`)

Generate UUIDs: v4 (random) or v7 (time-ordered: sorts by creation time, good for database keys). v7 IDs from one call are strictly increasing.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | choice: `v4`, `v7` | no | `"v4"` | v4 random, or v7 time-ordered. |
| `count` | integer | no | `1` | Number of UUIDs to generate (1–1000). |
| `uppercase` | boolean | no | `false` | Upper-case hex digits. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uuid` | string | The first (or only) UUID. |
| `uuids` | list of strings | Every UUID generated. |

### ULID (`ulid`)

Generate ULIDs: 26-character, time-ordered, URL-safe IDs (Crockford base32). ULIDs from one call are strictly increasing.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | integer | no | `1` | Number of ULIDs to generate (1–1000). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ulid` | string | The first (or only) ULID. |
| `ulids` | list of strings | Every ULID generated. |

### Hash (`hash`)

The SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-384 or SHA-1 digest of a text (UTF-8), as hex, base64 or base64url. For fingerprints, de-duplication and integrity checks; do not use plain hashes for passwords.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | text | no |  | The text to hash (UTF-8; empty text has a hash too). |
| `algorithm` | choice: `SHA-256`, `SHA-512`, `SHA-384`, `SHA-1` | no | `"SHA-256"` | Digest algorithm. |
| `encoding` | choice: `hex`, `base64`, `base64url` | no | `"hex"` | How the digest is written. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hash` | string |  |
| `algorithm` | string |  |

### HMAC signature (`hmac`)

Sign a message with HMAC using the hmac_key secret, or check a received signature (e.g. a webhook's X-Signature header) in constant time. The secret never enters the action's code.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | text | yes |  | The exact text to sign, e.g. the raw webhook body. |
| `algorithm` | choice: `SHA-256`, `SHA-512`, `SHA-384`, `SHA-1` | no | `"SHA-256"` | HMAC hash. |
| `encoding` | choice: `hex`, `base64`, `base64url` | no | `"hex"` | How the signature is written (match what the sender uses). |
| `expected` | string | no |  | Optional: a received signature to compare with (a sha256= prefix is ignored). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `signature` | string |  |
| `matches` | boolean | Whether Signature to check equals the computed signature (empty when none was given). |

### Encode (`encode`)

Encode text (UTF-8) as base64, base64url, hex or URL percent-encoding.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | text | yes |  | The text to encode. |
| `format` | choice: `base64`, `base64url`, `hex`, `url` | no | `"base64"` | Encoding. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | text |  |

### Decode (`decode`)

Decode base64, base64url, hex or URL percent-encoding back to text (UTF-8). Invalid input fails with a clear message.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | text | yes |  | The text to decode (whitespace is ignored for base64 and hex). |
| `format` | choice: `base64`, `base64url`, `hex`, `url` | no | `"base64"` | Encoding. |
| `plus_as_space` | boolean | no | `false` | URL format: decode + as a space (HTML form encoding). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | text |  |

### Random code (`random_code`)

Generate unbiased random codes from an alphabet: digits, letters and digits, hex, or no look-alikes (no 0/O, 1/I/L) for codes people read and type. Optional grouping such as XXXX-XXXX.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `length` | integer | no | `8` | Characters per code, not counting separators (1–256). |
| `alphabet` | choice: `no_lookalikes`, `digits`, `alphanumeric`, `alphanumeric_upper`, `letters_upper`, `hex`, `custom` | no | `"no_lookalikes"` | Which characters to use. |
| `custom_alphabet` | string | no |  | With Alphabet = Custom: the characters to use (at least 2). |
| `count` | integer | no | `1` | Number of codes to generate (1–1000). |
| `group_size` | integer | no | `0` | Insert the separator every N characters (0 = no grouping). |
| `separator` | string | no | `"-"` | Placed between groups. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | The first (or only) code. |
| `codes` | list of strings | Every code generated. |

### One-time code (`otp`)

A numeric one-time code (e.g. for email or SMS verification) with its expiry time and SHA-256 hash: store the hash, not the code, and compare hashes when the user types it.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `digits` | integer | no | `6` | 4–10 digits. |
| `expires_minutes` | integer | no | `10` | How long the code is valid. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | The code (keeps leading zeros). |
| `expires_at` | datetime | UTC instant. |
| `code_hash` | string | SHA-256 hex of the code. |

### Sign token (JWT) (`sign_token`)

Create a compact HS256 JSON Web Token signed with the token_secret secret: your claims plus iat, exp (from Expires in), optional iss / aud / sub and a unique jti.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claims` | object | no |  | The token's data, e.g. { "role": "approver", "request_id": "REQ-1042" }. |
| `expires_minutes` | integer | no | `60` | Lifetime of the token; 0 for no expiry. |
| `issuer` | string | no |  | Optional issuer claim. |
| `audience` | string | no |  | Optional audience claim. |
| `subject` | string | no |  | Optional subject claim, e.g. a user id. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jwt` | string | header.payload.signature |
| `expires_at` | datetime | UTC instant (empty without expiry). |
| `claims` | object | Every claim in the token. |

### Verify token (JWT) (`verify_token`)

Check an HS256 token signed with token_secret: the signature (constant-time), expiry (exp) and not-before (nbf) with a leeway, and optionally the issuer and audience. Invalid tokens return valid = false and a reason instead of failing the step.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jwt` | string | yes |  | The token (a "Bearer " prefix is ignored). |
| `issuer` | string | no |  | Optional: iss must equal this. |
| `audience` | string | no |  | Optional: aud must equal or contain this. |
| `leeway_seconds` | integer | no | `30` | Tolerance for exp and nbf. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `valid` | boolean |  |
| `reason` | string | Why the token is not valid: malformed, unsupported algorithm, bad signature, expired, not yet valid, issuer or audience does not match (empty when valid). |
| `claims` | object | The token's claims when the signature is valid (also when expired), else empty. |
| `expires_at` | datetime | From exp (empty without expiry). |

## Capabilities

Secrets only (no network, data tables or files):

- `hmac_key`: used by `hmac`. The host computes the HMAC with `secret://hmac_key`, so the key never enters the sandbox.
- `token_secret`: used by `sign_token` and `verify_token` (HS256, also computed on the host).

Both are optional: an administrator sets them in Extensibility → Workflow actions. An operation that needs an unset secret fails with a message naming it; the other operations work without any setup. Random values come from the host's cryptographic generator (ctx.crypto.randomBytes / randomUUID).

## Examples

**SHA-256 of "abc"** (`hash`)

```json
{
  "text": "abc",
  "algorithm": "SHA-256"
}
```

**Check a webhook signature** (`hmac`)

```json
{
  "message": "{\"event\":\"invoice.paid\",\"id\":\"evt_1042\"}",
  "expected": "sha256=1c1b1b59b8b80733797d06dae9234186bd3e41395f81d2773aa87f70daeaa4b3"
}
```

Signed with the hmac_key secret (the example uses the value "example-secret").

**Verify a signed token** (`verify_token`)

```json
{
  "jwt": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJ1c2VyLTQyIiwicm9sZSI6ImFwcHJvdmVyIiwiaXNzIjoidXNlcnRhc2tzIiwiYXVkIjoiYXBwcm92YWxzIn0.ViY7aLGdekI4TR6SYbUEvxrBc4VtgmtpczNL4qmy6YU",
  "issuer": "usertasks",
  "audience": "approvals"
}
```

Signed with token_secret = "example-secret".

**Base64 of UTF-8 text** (`encode`)

```json
{
  "text": "Hello, Wörld & friends",
  "format": "base64"
}
```

**Decode a URL parameter** (`decode`)

```json
{
  "text": "name%3DAroha%20Smith%26role%3Dapprover",
  "format": "url"
}
```

A sample workflow ships in `assets/workflows/`: it starts from the API or its start form, runs this action with default inputs and shows the outputs.

## Limits

- Each run has 5 seconds and 32 MB of sandbox memory; inputs and outputs are limited to 5 MB of JSON each.
- Up to 1,000 UUIDs, ULIDs or codes per run; codes up to 256 characters; text to hash, sign or encode up to 5,000,000 characters.
- UUID v7 and ULID values from one run are strictly increasing (a counter in the random bits within the same millisecond).
- Random codes use rejection sampling, so every character of the alphabet is equally likely.
- Tokens: HS256 only (other algorithms, including "none", are rejected); exp / nbf are checked with a leeway (default 30 seconds).
- Plain hashes are not for passwords; SHA-1 is offered for legacy systems only.

## Build and test

```sh
node gallery/actions/scripts/build.mjs crypto-ids
npx vitest run __tests__/gallery-action-crypto-ids.test.ts
```

actions.title: Data transform
actions.summary: Select by JSON path, map, filter, sort, group and aggregate, pivot, de-duplicate and join lists of records, and convert CSV to JSON and back.
actions.description:
Data transform reshapes lists of records inside a workflow, the work that otherwise takes loops and a chain of collection nodes. Pick values out of an API response with a JSON path (order.lines[*].sku), rename and nest fields, filter with conditions such as status = paid and amount >= 500, sort on several keys, group by one or more fields with count, sum, average, minimum, maximum and distinct counts, pivot values into columns or unpivot columns into rows, and remove duplicates by chosen fields.

Join combines two lists on matching keys (inner, left, right or full), for example orders with the managers of their regions, and reports what did not match. CSV to JSON parses spreadsheet exports to RFC 4180 (quoted fields, embedded commas and line breaks, header row, number and boolean inference) and JSON to CSV writes lists back out with chosen columns, CRLF line endings and protection against formula injection. Everything runs in the sandbox with no network or data access.
uses: Total and average order values per region before a weekly summary email
Join API results with a data table of owners and keep the unmatched rows for review
Import a CSV export, filter it and write a clean CSV back out
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
Drag Data transform onto a workflow, choose the function and map Items to a list (a data table query result, an API response path or a JSON variable).
Chain functions: map the {{prefix_items}} output of one step into the Items of the next, e.g. Filter, then Group & aggregate.
Try the included "Sales by region (sample)" workflow from the API or its start form: it filters paid orders, groups them by region and writes the totals as CSV.
actions.readme:
# Data transform (`ut_data`)

Reshape lists of records in UserTasks workflows: JSON path selection, field mapping, filtering, multi-key sorting, group by with aggregates, pivot and unpivot, de-duplication, joins and CSV to JSON conversion in both directions.

Official UserTasks workflow action, version 1.0.0. Source: `src/action.ts`; built module: `dist/action.js` (one self-contained ES module that runs in the UserTasks QuickJS sandbox).

## Operations

### Select (JSON path) (`select`)

Read a value from an object or list by path: a.b[0].c, items[-1] for the last item, items[*].name for every item's name (wildcards return a list).

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | json | yes |  | The object or list to read from. |
| `path` | string | yes |  | For example order.lines[0].sku or order.lines[*].sku ($. prefix optional). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | json | The value at the path (a list when the path has a wildcard; empty when not found). |
| `values` | list of jsons | Every value found, as a list. |
| `found` | boolean |  |
| `count` | integer | How many values were found. |

### Map fields (`map`)

Pick, rename and nest fields of every item: "customer.name as customer", "total" or { "from": "a.b", "to": "c", "default": 0 }.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | A list of objects (rows), e.g. a data table query result or a JSON array. |
| `fields` | list | yes |  | One per field: source path, optionally "as" a new name (a dotted name creates nested objects), or objects { from, to, default }. |
| `keep_other_fields` | boolean | no | `false` | Keep fields not listed (renamed ones move). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | The mapped items. |
| `count` | integer | How many items were returned. |

### Filter (`filter`)

Keep the items that match conditions: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte (numbers and dates compare as such), contains, not_contains, starts_with, ends_with, in, not_in, empty, not_empty; all must match or any.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | A list of objects (rows), e.g. a data table query result or a JSON array. |
| `conditions` | list of objects | yes |  | List of { "field": "status", "operator": "eq", "value": "paid" }; in / not_in take a list or comma-separated text. |
| `combine` | choice: `all`, `any` | no | `"all"` | Whether every condition or any condition must match. |
| `case_sensitive` | boolean | no | `false` | Compare text exactly (off: ignore case). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | The matching items, in their original order. |
| `count` | integer | How many items matched. |
| `removed` | integer | How many items did not match. |

### Sort (`sort`)

Sort by one or more keys, ascending or descending, comparing as numbers, text or dates (auto: numbers when both values are numeric). Stable; empty values sort last.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | A list of objects (rows), e.g. a data table query result or a JSON array. |
| `keys` | list | yes |  | In priority order: "amount desc", "-amount", "name asc text", or { "field", "direction": "asc" \| "desc", "type": "auto" \| "number" \| "text" \| "date" }. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | The sorted items. |
| `count` | integer | How many items were returned. |

### Group & aggregate (`group`)

Group items by one or more fields and compute aggregates per group: count, count_distinct, sum, avg, min, max, first, last or list. Each group row has the group fields, count and the aggregates.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | A list of objects (rows), e.g. a data table query result or a JSON array. |
| `group_by` | list of strings | yes |  | The field(s) to group by. |
| `aggregates` | list | no |  | "sum:amount", "avg(amount) as average", "count_distinct:product" or { "op": "sum", "field": "amount", "as": "total" }. The default name is op_field (sum_amount). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `groups` | list of objects | One row per group, in order of first appearance: the group fields, count and each aggregate. |
| `count` | integer |  |

### Pivot (`pivot`)

Turn values of one field into columns: one row per Rows key, one column per distinct Column value, aggregating Value (sum, count, avg, min, max, first, last).

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | A list of objects (rows), e.g. a data table query result or a JSON array. |
| `rows` | list of strings | yes |  | Field(s) that identify an output row. |
| `column` | string | yes |  | Field whose values become columns. |
| `value` | string | no |  | Field to aggregate in each cell (not needed for count). |
| `aggregate` | choice: `sum`, `count`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `first`, `last` | no | `"sum"` | How to combine several values in one cell. |
| `fill` | json | no |  | Value for a row/column with no items (default empty; e.g. 0). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | One row per Rows key with a property per column. |
| `columns` | list of strings | The column values, in order of first appearance. |
| `count` | integer | How many items were returned. |

### Unpivot (`unpivot`)

Turn columns into rows: for every item, one row per column with the column name and its value, keeping identifier fields.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | A list of objects with one column per measure. |
| `keep_fields` | list of strings | no |  | Identifier fields copied to every row. |
| `columns` | list of strings | no |  | The fields to turn into rows (default: every field not kept). |
| `name_field` | string | no | `"name"` | Field that receives the column name. |
| `value_field` | string | no | `"value"` | Field that receives the value. |
| `skip_empty` | boolean | no | `false` | Leave out rows whose value is empty. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | One row per item and column. |
| `count` | integer | How many items were returned. |

### Remove duplicates (`dedupe`)

Remove duplicate items, comparing chosen fields (or whole items, which also works for lists of plain values), keeping the first or the last of each.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list | yes |  | A list of objects or plain values. |
| `fields` | list of strings | no |  | Fields that make an item unique (default: the whole item). |
| `keep` | choice: `first`, `last` | no | `"first"` | Which duplicate to keep (the order of the list is kept). |
| `case_sensitive` | boolean | no | `true` | Off: "A@x.io" and "a@x.io" are duplicates. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of jsons | The unique items. |
| `count` | integer | How many items were returned. |
| `removed` | integer | How many duplicates were removed. |

### Join (`join`)

Combine two lists on matching keys (inner, left, right or full outer). Right fields whose names clash with left fields get the prefix right_ (or your own prefix on every right field).

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `left` | list of objects | yes |  | The main list of objects. |
| `right` | list of objects | yes |  | The list to look up. |
| `left_key` | list of strings | yes |  | Key field(s) in the left list. |
| `right_key` | list of strings | no |  | Key field(s) in the right list, in the same order (default: the left key names). |
| `type` | choice: `inner`, `left`, `right`, `full` | no | `"inner"` | Which unmatched rows to keep. |
| `right_prefix` | string | no |  | Optional prefix for every field from the right list. |
| `case_sensitive` | boolean | no | `true` | Off: keys match ignoring case. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | The joined rows (one per match). |
| `count` | integer | How many items were returned. |
| `unmatched_left` | integer | Left rows with no match. |
| `unmatched_right` | integer | Right rows with no match. |

### CSV to JSON (`csv_to_json`)

Parse CSV text (RFC 4180: quoted fields, "" escapes, line breaks in quotes) into a list of objects, using the header row for field names and inferring numbers and true/false.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `csv` | text | yes |  | The CSV text. |
| `delimiter` | string | no | `"auto"` | auto (detect), comma, semicolon, tab, pipe or the character(s). |
| `header` | boolean | no | `true` | The first row holds the field names (off: column_1, column_2, …). |
| `infer_types` | boolean | no | `true` | Turn numbers and true/false into numbers and booleans, empty cells into empty values (numbers with leading zeros stay text). |
| `trim` | boolean | no | `true` | Trim spaces around values. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | One object per data row. |
| `columns` | list of strings | The field names. |
| `count` | integer | How many data rows. |

### JSON to CSV (`json_to_csv`)

Write a list of objects as CSV (RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF line endings by default), with chosen columns and headers. Text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula is escaped by default.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | A list of objects (rows), e.g. a data table query result or a JSON array. |
| `columns` | list of strings | no |  | Fields to write, optionally "field as Header" (default: every field, in order of appearance). |
| `delimiter` | string | no | `","` | Field separator (tab for tab-separated). |
| `header` | boolean | no | `true` | Write the column names first. |
| `line_ending` | choice: `crlf`, `lf` | no | `"crlf"` | CRLF (RFC 4180, Excel) or LF. |
| `escape_formulas` | boolean | no | `true` | Prefix text starting with = + - @ with ' so spreadsheets do not run it (CSV injection). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `csv` | text |  |
| `columns` | list of strings | The header names. |
| `count` | integer | How many data rows. |

## Capabilities

None: pure computation. The action cannot reach the network, data tables, files or secrets.

## Examples

**Totals per region** (`group`)

```json

}
```

A sample workflow ships in `assets/workflows/`: it starts from the API or its start form, runs this action with default inputs and shows the outputs.

## Limits

- Each run has 5 seconds and 32 MB of sandbox memory; inputs and outputs are limited to 5 MB of JSON each.
- Lists hold up to 100,000 items; CSV input up to 5,000,000 characters.
- Comparisons: when both values are numeric (numbers or numeric text) they compare as numbers; otherwise as text (case-insensitive unless Case sensitive is on). Empty values never satisfy gt / gte / lt / lte and sort last.
- JSON to CSV escapes text starting with = + - @ by default (CSV injection); turn Escape formulas off for data that is never opened in a spreadsheet.

## Build and test

```sh
node gallery/actions/scripts/build.mjs data-transform
npx vitest run __tests__/gallery-action-data-transform.test.ts
```

actions.title: Dates & business calendar
actions.summary: Business days around holidays, SLA due times in working hours across time zones and DST, durations and ages, recurring schedules and fiscal periods.
actions.description:
Dates & business calendar handles the date rules that decide deadlines. Add or subtract business days around weekends and your holiday list, and compute an SLA due time from a start moment and a number of working hours: only working hours on working days count, in the time zone of the team, with daylight-saving changes handled because working hours are wall-clock times. The result comes back as a UTC instant and as local time with its offset.

It also measures durations (calendar days, business days, hours, a readable "2 years, 3 months" text and an exact age), converts a moment between time zones, lists the next occurrences of a schedule such as "the last Friday of every month at 16:00 London time", and finds the fiscal year, quarter and period of a date for a fiscal year that starts in any month, with the period, quarter and year boundaries and a label like FY2027 Q2.
uses: Set a due date 8 working hours after a ticket arrives, in the support team's time zone
Pay an invoice 10 business days after approval, skipping public holidays
Tag records with the fiscal year and quarter for reporting
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
Drag Dates & business calendar onto a workflow, choose the function and map its inputs; keep holidays in a data table or variable and map the list into Holidays.
Use the outputs from the data picker, e.g. {{sla_due}} for a Set SLA or Pause Until step, or {{fiscal_label}} in a title.
Try the included "Business-hours SLA (sample)" workflow from the API or its start form: it computes a due time in Pacific/Auckland working hours and the business days until then.
actions.readme:
# Dates & business calendar (`ut_dates`)

Date and business-calendar logic for UserTasks workflows: business days around weekends and holidays, SLA due times in working hours (time zone and DST aware), durations and ages, time zone conversion, recurring schedules and fiscal periods.

Official UserTasks workflow action, version 1.0.0. Source: `src/action.ts`; built module: `dist/action.js` (one self-contained ES module that runs in the UserTasks QuickJS sandbox).

## Operations

### Add business days (`add_business_days`)

Add (or with a negative number, subtract) business days to a date, skipping weekends and holidays. Adding 0 returns the date itself, or the next business day when it falls on a weekend or holiday.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | yes |  | The starting date (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `days` | integer | yes |  | How many business days to add; negative to go back. |
| `weekend_days` | list of strings | no | `["Saturday","Sunday"]` | Days that are not business days (names such as Saturday, or ISO numbers 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday). |
| `holidays` | list of strings | no |  | Dates that are not business days, as YYYY-MM-DD (a list, or one per line). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | The resulting business day. |
| `weekday` | string | Monday … Sunday. |
| `calendar_days` | integer | Calendar days between the start and the result (negative when going back). |

### SLA due time (`sla_due`)

The moment a number of working hours after a start time runs out, counting only working hours on working days in a time zone and skipping holidays. Daylight-saving changes are handled: working hours are wall-clock times.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | datetime | yes |  | When the clock starts (ISO 8601). Without Z or an offset it is local time in Time zone. |
| `hours` | number | yes |  | The SLA in working hours (decimals allowed, e.g. 0.5). |
| `working_hours` | string | no | `"09:00-17:00"` | Start and end of the working day, e.g. 09:00-17:00 (use 00:00-24:00 for round the clock). |
| `working_days` | list of strings | no | `["Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday"]` | Weekdays that have working hours (names or ISO numbers 1–7). |
| `time_zone` | string | no | `"UTC"` | IANA time zone of the working hours and holidays. |
| `holidays` | list of strings | no |  | Dates that are not business days, as YYYY-MM-DD (a list, or one per line). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `due` | datetime | The due moment as an ISO 8601 UTC instant. |
| `due_local` | string | The due moment in the time zone, with its offset, e.g. 2026-11-09T14:30:00+13:00. |
| `due_date` | date |  |
| `start_local` | string | The start in the time zone, with its offset. |
| `calendar_hours` | number | Elapsed real time from start to due, in hours. |

### Duration / age (`duration`)

The time between two dates or date-times: calendar days, business days, hours and minutes, a readable text and the age in years, months and days. Negative when To is before From.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | datetime | yes |  | Date (YYYY-MM-DD) or date-time. |
| `to` | datetime | no |  | Date or date-time; empty for now. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | `"UTC"` | Time zone for dates and times without an offset, and for counting calendar days. |
| `weekend_days` | list of strings | no | `["Saturday","Sunday"]` | Days that are not business days (names such as Saturday, or ISO numbers 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday). |
| `holidays` | list of strings | no |  | Dates that are not business days, as YYYY-MM-DD (a list, or one per line). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `days` | integer | Whole calendar days. |
| `business_days` | integer | Business days after From up to and including To. |
| `hours` | number | Elapsed hours (2 decimals). |
| `minutes` | integer | Elapsed whole minutes. |
| `human` | string | For example "36 years, 3 months, 17 days" or "2 hours, 15 minutes". |
| `age_years` | integer | Whole years (age). |
| `age_months` | integer | Months after the whole years. |
| `age_days` | integer | Days after the whole months. |

### Convert time zone (`convert_timezone`)

Show a moment in another time zone: the UTC instant, the local date-time with its offset, date, time and weekday.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `datetime` | datetime | yes |  | ISO 8601. Without Z or an offset it is read in From zone. |
| `from_zone` | string | no | `"UTC"` | IANA time zone of a date-time without an offset. |
| `to_zone` | string | yes |  | IANA time zone to show the moment in. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iso` | datetime |  |
| `local` | string | With its offset, e.g. 2026-11-03T03:00:00+13:00. |
| `local_date` | date |  |
| `local_time` | string | HH:mm. |
| `weekday` | string |  |
| `offset` | string | For example +13:00. |
| `offset_minutes` | integer |  |

### Next occurrences (`next_occurrence`)

The next dates of a recurring schedule: daily, weekly on chosen days, monthly on a day of the month or the nth weekday (e.g. last Friday), or yearly, every N periods, at a time of day in a time zone.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frequency` | choice: `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `yearly` | no | `"weekly"` | How often it repeats. |
| `interval` | integer | no | `1` | Repeat every N days / weeks / months / years. |
| `days_of_week` | list of strings | no |  | Weekly: the days (names or ISO numbers); default the weekday of Start. |
| `day_of_month` | integer | no |  | Monthly / yearly: 1–31 (later than the month has = its last day) or -1 for the last day; default the day of Start. |
| `nth_week` | choice: `none`, `first`, `second`, `third`, `fourth`, `last` | no | `"none"` | Monthly / yearly: instead of a day of the month, the first … fourth or last Weekday. |
| `weekday` | string | no |  | With Nth weekday: Monday … Sunday. |
| `month` | integer | no |  | Yearly: 1–12; default the month of Start. |
| `time` | string | no | `"09:00"` | Local time of each occurrence (HH:mm). |
| `time_zone` | string | no | `"UTC"` | IANA time zone of the schedule. |
| `after` | datetime | no |  | List occurrences after this moment; empty for now. |
| `start` | date | no |  | First possible date of the schedule (the anchor for Every N); default the date of After. |
| `count` | integer | no | `5` | Number of occurrences to return (1–100). |
| `exclude_dates` | list of strings | no |  | Dates (YYYY-MM-DD) to leave out, e.g. holidays. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `next` | datetime | The next occurrence (UTC instant); empty when none was found. |
| `next_local` | string | With its offset. |
| `occurrences` | list of datetimes | UTC instants, in order. |
| `occurrences_local` | list of strings | Local date-times with offsets. |

### Fiscal period (`fiscal_period`)

The fiscal year, quarter and period (month) of a date for a fiscal year starting in any month, with the start and end dates of the period, quarter and year and a label such as FY2027 Q2.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | no |  | The date; empty for today (in Time zone). |
| `start_month` | integer | no | `7` | 1 = January … 12 = December, e.g. 7 for July (Australia, NZ public sector), 4 for April (UK, India, Japan, Canada). |
| `year_naming` | choice: `end`, `start` | no | `"end"` | The calendar year in which the fiscal year ends (FY2027 = July 2026–June 2027) or starts. |
| `time_zone` | string | no | `"UTC"` | For "today" when Date is empty. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fiscal_year` | integer |  |
| `quarter` | integer | 1–4. |
| `period` | integer | Month of the fiscal year, 1–12. |
| `label` | string | For example FY2027 Q2. |
| `period_label` | string | For example FY2027 P05. |
| `period_start` | date |  |
| `period_end` | date |  |
| `quarter_start` | date |  |
| `quarter_end` | date |  |
| `year_start` | date |  |
| `year_end` | date |  |
| `day_of_year` | integer | 1 on the first day. |

## Capabilities

None: pure computation. Time zone rules come from the host's ctx.intl helpers (IANA time zone database); the action cannot reach the network, data tables, files or secrets.

## Examples

**8 working hours from Friday afternoon** (`sla_due`)

```json
{
  "start": "2026-11-06T15:30:00",
  "hours": 8,
  "working_hours": "09:00-17:00",
  "time_zone": "Pacific/Auckland"
}
```

1.5 hours on Friday, the rest on Monday.

**3 business days over Christmas** (`add_business_days`)

```json
{
  "date": "2026-12-23",
  "days": 3,
  "holidays": [
    "2026-12-25",
    "2026-12-28",
    "2027-01-01"
  ]
}
```

**Fiscal quarter (year from July)** (`fiscal_period`)

```json
{
  "date": "2026-11-01",
  "start_month": 7
}
```

**Last Friday of the month at 16:00 London** (`next_occurrence`)

```json
{
  "frequency": "monthly",
  "nth_week": "last",
  "weekday": "Friday",
  "time": "16:00",
  "time_zone": "Europe/London",
  "after": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z",
  "count": 3
}
```

**Age on a date** (`duration`)

```json
{
  "from": "1990-07-15",
  "to": "2026-11-01"
}
```

A sample workflow ships in `assets/workflows/`: it starts from the API or its start form, runs this action with default inputs and shows the outputs.

## Limits

- Each run has 5 seconds and 32 MB of sandbox memory; inputs and outputs are limited to 5 MB of JSON each.
- Time zones are IANA names; an unknown zone is an error. Date-times without Z or an offset are read as wall-clock time in the operation's time zone.
- Business days and SLA searches look at most 10 years ahead; schedules look up to 200 years ahead and return at most 100 occurrences.
- Monthly schedules on day 29–31 fall on the last day of shorter months. Ages count a month from the same day of the month (Jan 31 + 1 month = Feb 28/29).

## Build and test

```sh
node gallery/actions/scripts/build.mjs date-business-calendar
npx vitest run __tests__/gallery-action-date-business-calendar.test.ts
```

actions.title: Math & statistics
actions.summary: Safe formulas with variables, exact rounding, statistics and percentiles, compound interest, loan schedules and unit conversion in one workflow step.
actions.description:
Math & statistics gives workflows the numeric operations that otherwise take a chain of Calculate Value nodes or a spreadsheet. Evaluate a formula such as (price * qty) * (1 + tax_rate) against an object of variables with a real parser (never eval), round with half-up, banker's, floor or ceiling rules that are decimal-exact, and summarise a list of numbers or a field of a list of rows: count, sum, mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation and percentiles.

The finance operations return what approvals and customer letters need. Loan schedule computes the monthly payment, each period's interest and principal, totals and the payoff date, with money in cents so the last payment brings the balance to exactly zero; Compound interest grows savings with regular contributions and returns a year-by-year table. Convert units covers length, mass, volume, temperature, area, speed, data size and time. Everything runs in the sandbox with no network, data or secret access.
uses: Show a loan or lease repayment schedule in a quote or approval task
Summarise order values or response times (mean, median, 90th percentile) in a scheduled report
Compute totals with tax and discounts from form fields using one readable formula
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
Drag Math & statistics onto a workflow, choose the function (Evaluate formula, Loan schedule, …) and map its inputs from variables or form fields.
Use the outputs from the data picker, e.g. {{loan_payment}} or loop over {{loan_schedule}} rows; each output is typed (number, date, list of objects).
Try the included "Loan repayment schedule (sample)" workflow: run it from the API or its start form with no input to see a 60-month schedule.

# Math & statistics (`ut_math`)

Numeric building blocks for UserTasks workflows: a safe formula evaluator with variables (its own parser, never `eval`), decimal-exact rounding in six modes, descriptive statistics and percentiles over a list of numbers or a field of a list of objects, compound interest with contributions, monthly loan amortisation schedules and unit conversion.

Official UserTasks workflow action, version 1.0.0. Source: `src/action.ts`; built module: `dist/action.js` (one self-contained ES module that runs in the UserTasks QuickJS sandbox).

## Operations

### Evaluate formula (`evaluate`)

Evaluate an arithmetic formula with + - * / % ^ and parentheses, variables from an object and the functions abs, round, floor, ceil, sqrt, min, max, pow, log, ln, exp, sin, cos and tan (constants pi and e). Never runs code.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `expression` | string | yes |  | For example (price * qty) * (1 + tax_rate) - discount. Variable names may be dotted paths into Variables (order.total). ^ is power, % is remainder; log(x) is base 10, log(x, b) base b, ln(x) natural. |
| `variables` | object | no |  | The values the formula uses, as an object: { "price": 19.99, "qty": 3 }. Numeric text is accepted. |
| `decimals` | integer | no |  | Optional: round the result to this many decimal places (half up). Leave empty for the full result. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | number | The value of the formula. |

### Round (`round`)

Round a number to a number of decimal places with an explicit rounding mode. Decimal-exact: 1.005 rounds to 1.01.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | yes |  | The number to round. |
| `decimals` | integer | no | `0` | Decimal places (0 for whole numbers; negative rounds to tens, hundreds…). |
| `mode` | choice: `half_up`, `half_even`, `up`, `down`, `floor`, `ceil` | no | `"half_up"` | How to round a value that sits between two results. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | number | The rounded number. |

### Statistics (`stats`)

Descriptive statistics for a list of numbers (or a field of a list of objects): count, sum, mean, min, max, median, mode, variance, standard deviation and range.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | list | yes |  | The numbers: a list of numbers (or numeric text), or a list of objects with Field naming the number. Blank entries are skipped. |
| `field` | string | no |  | When Values is a list of objects: the property holding the number (dotted paths such as amount.total work). |
| `variance_type` | choice: `sample`, `population` | no | `"sample"` | Sample (n - 1, for a sample of a larger population) or population (n, for the whole set). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | integer | How many numbers there are (blank entries are skipped). |
| `sum` | number |  |
| `mean` | number | The average (empty when there are no numbers). |
| `min` | number |  |
| `max` | number |  |
| `median` | number | The middle value (the average of the two middle values for an even count). |
| `mode` | number | The most frequent value (the smallest if several tie); empty when no value repeats. |
| `variance` | number | Sample variance needs at least 2 numbers. |
| `stddev` | number |  |
| `range` | number | Maximum minus minimum. |

### Percentile (`percentile`)

The p-th percentile of a list of numbers, with linear interpolation between the closest ranks (the same as Excel PERCENTILE.INC).

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | list | yes |  | The numbers: a list of numbers (or numeric text), or a list of objects with Field naming the number. Blank entries are skipped. |
| `field` | string | no |  | When Values is a list of objects: the property holding the number (dotted paths such as amount.total work). |
| `p` | number | yes |  | From 0 to 100: 50 is the median, 90 the 90th percentile. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | The percentile. |
| `count` | integer | How many numbers were used. |

### Compound interest (`compound_interest`)

Grow a starting amount with compound interest and optional regular contributions; returns the future value and a year-by-year schedule.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principal` | number | yes |  | The amount invested at the start. |
| `annual_rate` | number | yes |  | Nominal annual interest rate in percent, e.g. 5 for 5%. |
| `years` | integer | yes |  | How many years (1 to 100). |
| `compounds_per_year` | integer | no | `12` | 1 yearly, 4 quarterly, 12 monthly, 52 weekly, 365 daily. |
| `contribution` | number | no | `0` | Optional amount added every compounding period (e.g. monthly when compounding monthly). |
| `contribution_timing` | choice: `end`, `start` | no | `"end"` | Whether contributions are added at the start or the end of each period. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `future_value` | number | The balance at the end, rounded to 2 decimals. |
| `total_contributions` | number | The starting amount plus every contribution. |
| `interest_earned` | number | Future value minus total contributions. |
| `schedule` | list of objects | One row per year. Each item: `year` (integer), `contributions` (number), `interest` (number), `balance` (number). |

### Loan schedule (`loan_schedule`)

Monthly amortisation schedule for a fixed-rate loan: the payment (P·r / (1 − (1 + r)^−n)), each period's interest and principal, the balance, totals and the payoff date. Extra payments shorten the loan.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principal` | number | yes |  | The amount borrowed. |
| `annual_rate` | number | yes |  | Nominal annual interest rate in percent (0 for an interest-free loan). |
| `term_months` | integer | yes |  | Number of monthly payments (1 to 600), e.g. 360 for 30 years. |
| `start_date` | date | no |  | Optional: the date of the first payment; later payments fall on the same day of each month (the last day in shorter months). |
| `extra_payment` | number | no | `0` | Optional extra principal paid with every payment. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payment` | number | The regular payment (the last one may be smaller). |
| `total_interest` | number |  |
| `total_paid` | number | Principal plus interest. |
| `number_of_payments` | integer | Fewer than the term when extra payments are made. |
| `payoff_date` | date | The date of the last payment (empty without a first payment date). |
| `schedule` | list of objects | One row per payment. Each item: `period` (integer), `date` (date), `payment` (number), `principal` (number), `interest` (number), `balance` (number). |

### Convert units (`convert_units`)

Convert a value between units of length, mass, volume, temperature, area, speed, data size and time.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | yes |  | The amount to convert. |
| `from` | string | yes |  | Symbol or name: mm cm m km in ft yd mi nmi · mg g kg t oz lb st · ml l m3 tsp tbsp floz cup pt qt gal gal_uk · C F K · m2 km2 ha ac ft2 · m/s km/h mph kn · bit B kB MB GB TB KiB MiB GiB Mb Gb · ms s min h d wk mo yr. |
| `to` | string | yes |  | A unit of the same kind as From unit. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | number | The converted value (12 significant digits). |
| `category` | string | length, mass, volume, temperature, area, speed, data or time. |
| `from_unit` | string |  |
| `to_unit` | string |  |

## Capabilities

None: pure computation. The action cannot reach the network, data tables, files or secrets.

## Examples

**Order total with tax and discount** (`evaluate`)

```json
{
  "expression": "(price * qty) * (1 + tax_rate) - discount",
  "variables": {
    "price": 19.99,
    "qty": 3,
    "tax_rate": 0.15,
    "discount": 5
  },
  "decimals": 2
}
```

Variables come from an object; the result is rounded to 2 decimals.

**Five-year car loan** (`loan_schedule`)

```json
{
  "principal": 25000,
  "annual_rate": 7.9,
  "term_months": 60,
  "start_date": "2026-12-01"
}
```

**Summary of response times** (`stats`)

```json
{
  "values": [
    {
      "minutes": 12
    },
    {
      "minutes": 15
    },
    {
      "minutes": 15
    },
    {
      "minutes": 18
    },
    {
      "minutes": 21
    },
    {
      "minutes": 30
    }
  ],
  "field": "minutes"
}
```

**Banker's rounding** (`round`)

```json
{
  "value": 2.345,
  "decimals": 2,
  "mode": "half_even"
}
```

Half even rounds 2.345 to 2.34 and 2.355 to 2.36.

**Marathon in kilometres** (`convert_units`)

```json
{
  "value": 26.2,
  "from": "mi",
  "to": "km"
}
```

A sample workflow ships in `assets/workflows/`: it starts from the API or its start form, runs this action with default inputs and shows the outputs.

## Limits

- Each run has 5 seconds and 32 MB of sandbox memory; inputs and outputs are limited to 5 MB of JSON each.
- Formulas: up to 4,000 characters and 64 levels of nesting; a result that is not a finite number (overflow, 0/0) is an error.
- Loan schedules: up to 600 monthly payments. Interest is computed per period on the balance in cents and rounded half up; the last payment is adjusted so the balance ends at exactly 0.
- Compound interest: 1 to 100 years, up to 365 compounding periods a year.
- Unit conversion results have 12 significant digits. A month is 1/12 of a Gregorian year (30.436875 days) and a year 365.2425 days.

## Build and test

```sh
node gallery/actions/scripts/build.mjs math-statistics
npx vitest run __tests__/gallery-action-math-statistics.test.ts
```
