actions.summary: Slugs, case conversion, {{placeholder}} templates, truncation, extraction, fuzzy matching, word counts and masking for workflow text.
actions.description:
Text toolkit covers the text clean-up and reshaping that workflows do all the time. Make URL- and file-safe slugs from titles (accents folded, & spelled out), convert between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, CONSTANT_CASE, Title Case and Sentence case, fill {{placeholder}} templates from an object with nested paths and fallbacks, shorten text for previews without cutting words in half, and pull values out from between markers.

For messy input there is fuzzy matching: Levenshtein distance, normalised similarity and Jaro-Winkler between two values, or the best match of a typed name in a list of candidates with a threshold, which is useful for matching free-text supplier or customer names to your records. Word count returns words, characters, sentences, paragraphs and reading time, and Mask hides card numbers, account numbers or email addresses before they are logged or sent. Everything runs in the sandbox with no network or data access.
uses: Match a supplier name typed on a form to the closest name in your vendor list
Build a notification from a template with the requester's and record's fields
Mask account or card numbers before writing them to a log, task or email
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
Drag Text toolkit onto a workflow, choose the function and map its inputs from variables or form fields.
Use the outputs from the data picker, e.g. {{slug_slug}} or {{match_best_match}}.
Try the included "Text clean-up (sample)" workflow from the API or its start form: it slugs a title, fuzzy-matches a name and masks an account number.
actions.readme:
# Text toolkit (`ut_text`)

Text operations for UserTasks workflows: slugs, case conversion, `{{placeholder}}` templates, truncation, extraction between markers, fuzzy matching (Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler), word counts and masking of sensitive values.

Official UserTasks workflow action, version 1.0.0. Source: `src/action.ts`; built module: `dist/action.js` (one self-contained ES module that runs in the UserTasks QuickJS sandbox).

## Operations

### Slugify (`slugify`)

Turn text into a URL- and file-name-safe slug: accents removed (é → e, ß → ss), & becomes "and", everything else that is not a letter or digit becomes the separator.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  | The text to turn into a slug. |
| `separator` | string | no | `"-"` | Placed between words (up to 3 punctuation characters). |
| `lowercase` | boolean | no | `true` | Lowercase the slug. |
| `max_length` | integer | no | `0` | Optional: cut the slug to this many characters, at a word boundary when possible (0 = no limit). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slug` | string | For example creme-brulee-and-cafe-menu-2026. |

### Change case (`change_case`)

Convert between camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, CONSTANT_CASE, Title Case, Sentence case, UPPER and lower. Words are split on spaces, punctuation and case changes (parseHTTPResponse → parse HTTP response).

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  | The text or identifier to convert. |
| `case` | choice: `camel`, `pascal`, `snake`, `kebab`, `constant`, `title`, `sentence`, `upper`, `lower` | no | `"snake"` | The case to convert to. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | string |  |

### Fill template (`template`)

Replace {{name}} placeholders with values from an object. Paths reach nested values ({{customer.name}}, {{items[0].sku}}) and {{name | fallback}} gives a default. Objects and lists are inserted as JSON.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template` | text | yes |  | Text with {{placeholders}}. |
| `data` | object | no |  | The values, as an object. |
| `missing` | choice: `keep`, `blank`, `error` | no | `"keep"` | Keep the {{placeholder}}, leave it blank, or fail the step. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | text | The filled-in text. |
| `missing` | list of strings | Placeholder paths that had no value (and no fallback). |
| `replaced` | integer | How many placeholders were filled. |

### Truncate (`truncate`)

Shorten text to a number of characters or words and add an ellipsis. In character mode the result, ellipsis included, fits the length and does not cut a word in half when it can avoid it.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | text | yes |  | The text to shorten. |
| `length` | integer | yes |  | Maximum characters (or words). |
| `by` | choice: `chars`, `words` | no | `"chars"` | Count characters or words. |
| `ellipsis` | string | no | `"…"` | Added when the text is cut; enter none for no ellipsis. |
| `preserve_words` | boolean | no | `true` | In character mode, cut at the last space instead of mid-word. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `result` | text |  |
| `truncated` | boolean | Whether the text was shortened. |

### Extract between (`extract_between`)

Find the text between a start and an end marker (the first match or all of them). Leave the start empty to read from the beginning, or the end empty to read to the end.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | text | yes |  | The text to search. |
| `start` | string | no |  | Text just before the value. |
| `end` | string | no |  | Text just after the value. |
| `all` | boolean | no | `false` | Return every match instead of the first. |
| `include_markers` | boolean | no | `false` | Keep the start and end markers in the result. |
| `case_sensitive` | boolean | no | `true` | Match the markers exactly (off: ignore case). |
| `trim` | boolean | no | `true` | Trim spaces around each match. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | The first match (empty when none). |
| `matches` | list of strings | Every match (one when All matches is off). |
| `count` | integer |  |
| `found` | boolean |  |

### Similarity / fuzzy match (`similarity`)

Compare a value with another (Levenshtein distance, normalised similarity 0–1 and Jaro-Winkler) and/or find its best fuzzy match in a list of candidates, with a threshold.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | yes |  | The text to compare or look up. |
| `compare_to` | string | no |  | Optional: a second text to compare with. |
| `candidates` | list | no |  | Optional: a list of texts to find the best match in. |
| `threshold` | number | no | `0.8` | Score (0–1) at or above which it counts as a match. |
| `method` | choice: `jaro_winkler`, `levenshtein` | no | `"jaro_winkler"` | Score used for the candidate list and the threshold. |
| `case_sensitive` | boolean | no | `false` | Off: compare ignoring case (spaces are always normalised). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `distance` | integer | Levenshtein distance between Value and Compare to (empty without Compare to). |
| `similarity` | number | 1 − distance / longer length (0–1). |
| `jaro_winkler` | number | Jaro-Winkler score (0–1). |
| `best_match` | string | The candidate with the highest score (empty without candidates). |
| `best_score` | number |  |
| `best_index` | integer | Position of the best match in the list (from 0; −1 when none). |
| `matched` | boolean | Whether the score reaches the threshold. |

### Word count (`word_count`)

Count words, characters (with and without spaces), sentences and paragraphs, and estimate the reading time.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | text | no |  | The text to count (empty text counts as 0). |
| `words_per_minute` | integer | no | `200` | Words per minute for the reading time. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `words` | integer |  |
| `characters` | integer |  |
| `characters_no_spaces` | integer |  |
| `sentences` | integer |  |
| `paragraphs` | integer |  |
| `reading_minutes` | integer | Rounded up; 0 for empty text. |

### Mask (`mask`)

Hide part of a sensitive value: keep the last or first N characters, mask everything, or mask an email address (a***@example.com). Spaces and dashes can stay visible so the shape remains readable.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | yes |  | The value to mask. |
| `mode` | choice: `keep_last`, `keep_first`, `email`, `all` | no | `"keep_last"` | What to keep visible. |
| `keep` | integer | no | `4` | N for Keep the last / first N (never more than half of the value is shown). |
| `mask_char` | string | no | `"*"` | The character that replaces hidden ones. |
| `preserve_separators` | boolean | no | `true` | Leave spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, + and brackets unmasked. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `masked` | string |  |

## Capabilities

None: pure computation. The action cannot reach the network, data tables, files or secrets.

## Examples

**A slug from a title** (`slugify`)

```json
{
  "text": "Crème brûlée & Café Menu 2026!"
}
```

**Best match for a misspelt name** (`similarity`)

```json
{
  "value": "Jon Smyth",
  "candidates": [
    "John Smith",
    "Joan Smythe",
    "Jonas Schmidt"
  ],
  "threshold": 0.85
}
```

**Fill a message template** (`template`)

```json
{
  "template": "Hi {{customer.first_name}}, your order {{order.id}} ships {{order.ship_date | soon}}.",
  "data": {
    "customer": {
      "first_name": "Aroha"
    },
    "order": {
      "id": "SO-1042"
    }
  }
}
```

order.ship_date is missing, so its fallback "soon" is used.

**Mask a card number** (`mask`)

```json
{
  "value": "4111 1111 1111 1111",
  "mode": "keep_last",
  "keep": 4
}
```

**Identifier to camelCase** (`change_case`)

```json
{
  "text": "customer order ID",
  "case": "camel"
}
```

A sample workflow ships in `assets/workflows/`: it starts from the API or its start form, runs this action with default inputs and shows the outputs.

## Limits

- Each run has 5 seconds and 32 MB of sandbox memory; inputs and outputs are limited to 5 MB of JSON each.
- Text inputs: up to 1,000,000 characters (similarity: 10,000 characters per value and 10,000 candidates).
- Lengths and positions count Unicode code points, so accented letters and emoji count as one character.
- Slugs contain ASCII letters and digits only: letters from scripts without an ASCII form (Cyrillic, CJK, …) are dropped.

## Build and test

```sh
node gallery/actions/scripts/build.mjs text-toolkit
npx vitest run __tests__/gallery-action-text-toolkit.test.ts
```

actions.title: Validation & formatting
actions.summary: Validate IBAN, BIC, cards, emails, phones, postcodes and national IDs with check digits; format and parse numbers, money and phone numbers by locale.
actions.description:
Validation & formatting checks identifiers before they reach your finance, HR or CRM systems. It validates IBANs (country length and mod-97 check digits), BIC / SWIFT codes, payment card numbers (Luhn and issuer), email syntax, phone numbers (normalised to E.164 with a default country), postcodes for 26 countries and 13 national ID and tax number schemes such as the US SSN, UK National Insurance number, NZ IRD and NHI numbers, German Steuer-ID, French NIR and Indian Aadhaar. Each result has a valid flag, the normalised value to store and a plain-language reason when it fails; Validate many checks a whole form in one step.

The formatting side shows numbers the way each audience reads them: grouping and decimals per locale, percentages, compact numbers and currencies with their usual decimals, symbols or codes, and accounting brackets for negatives. Parse number reads amounts typed in any locale ("1.234,56 €" in German is 1234.56) and Format phone writes numbers as E.164, international or national. All checks run in the sandbox with no network access; they prove a value is well-formed, not that an account exists.
uses: Check a supplier's IBAN, BIC and tax number before creating them in the ERP
Normalise customer phone numbers to E.164 for SMS and CRM sync
Show amounts in the customer's currency and locale in emails and documents
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
Drag Validation & formatting onto a workflow after a form or API step, choose Validate (or Validate many for several fields) and map the values.
Branch on {{check_valid}} or {{check_all_valid}} with a Branch by Condition step, and store {{check_normalized}} instead of the typed value.
Try the included "Supplier bank details check (sample)" workflow from the API or its start form: it validates an IBAN, BIC, email and phone and formats the first payment amount.
actions.readme:
# Validation & formatting (`ut_validate`)

Validation of identifiers (IBAN, BIC, payment cards, email, phone, postcodes, national IDs and tax numbers) with normalised values and plain-language reasons, and locale-aware formatting and parsing of numbers, currencies and phone numbers.

Official UserTasks workflow action, version 1.0.0. Source: `src/action.ts`; built module: `dist/action.js` (one self-contained ES module that runs in the UserTasks QuickJS sandbox).

## Operations

### Validate (`validate`)

Check one value: iban, bic, card, email, phone, postcode or national_id. Returns valid, the normalised value, the reason it is invalid and type-specific details (card issuer, IBAN country, phone country code, formatted ID, …).

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | choice: `iban`, `bic`, `card`, `email`, `phone`, `postcode`, `national_id` | yes | `"email"` | What the value is. |
| `value` | string | yes |  | The value to check (spaces and dashes are allowed where usual). |
| `country` | string | no |  | Postcode: the ISO country (US, GB, CA, AU, NZ, DE, FR, NL, IE, ES, IT, …). Phone: the default country (ISO code or calling code such as 64) for numbers without +. |
| `id_type` | choice: `us_ssn`, `uk_nino`, `ca_sin`, `au_tfn`, `nz_ird`, `nz_nhi`, `de_tax_id`, `fr_nir`, `es_dni`, `it_fiscal_code`, `nl_bsn`, `in_aadhaar`, `sg_nric` | no |  | For national_id: which scheme. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `valid` | boolean |  |
| `normalized` | string | The value in its standard form (IBAN without spaces, E.164 phone, upper-case postcode with standard spacing, digits-only card number, …). |
| `reason` | string | Why the value is invalid (empty when valid). |
| `details` | object | Type-specific facts: iban country, bban and formatted; bic bank_code, country, branch; card issuer, last4, masked; email local, domain; phone country_code, national_number, international; national_id formatted. |

### Validate many (`validate_many`)

Check a list of { type, value } entries at once (e.g. every field of an onboarding form) and get one result per entry plus whether all are valid.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | list of objects | yes |  | List of { "type": "email", "value": "…", "name"?: "label", "country"?: "NZ", "id_type"?: "nz_ird" }. |
| `country` | string | no |  | Used for phone and postcode entries without their own country. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | list of objects | One per item, in order. Each item: `name` (string), `type` (string), `value` (string), `valid` (boolean), `normalized` (string), `reason` (string). |
| `all_valid` | boolean |  |
| `valid_count` | integer |  |
| `invalid_count` | integer |  |

### Format number (`format_number`)

Format a number for a locale: grouping and decimal separators, percent (0.25 → 25%), currency, or compact (1.2K) notation.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | yes |  | The number. For percent, 0.25 is 25%. |
| `locale` | string | no | `"en-US"` | BCP 47 locale, e.g. en-US, en-NZ, de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP. |
| `style` | choice: `decimal`, `percent`, `currency` | no | `"decimal"` | Plain number, percent or currency. |
| `currency` | string | no |  | For the currency style: ISO 4217 code (USD, EUR, NZD, JPY, …). |
| `minimum_fraction_digits` | integer | no |  | Optional: at least this many decimal places. |
| `maximum_fraction_digits` | integer | no |  | Optional: at most this many decimal places (rounded). |
| `use_grouping` | boolean | no | `true` | Group digits (1,234,567). |
| `notation` | choice: `standard`, `compact`, `scientific`, `engineering` | no | `"standard"` | Standard, compact (1.2M), scientific or engineering. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `formatted` | string |  |

### Format currency (`format_currency`)

Format an amount of money for a locale and currency, with the currency's usual decimals (JPY has none) and symbol, code or name.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | yes |  | The amount. |
| `currency` | string | yes |  | ISO 4217 code (USD, EUR, GBP, NZD, AUD, JPY, …). |
| `locale` | string | no | `"en-US"` | BCP 47 locale, e.g. en-US, en-NZ, de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP. |
| `display` | choice: `symbol`, `narrowSymbol`, `code`, `name` | no | `"symbol"` | Symbol ($), narrow symbol, ISO code (NZD) or name (New Zealand dollars). |
| `accounting` | boolean | no | `false` | Show negative amounts in brackets, e.g. ($1,234.50). |
| `minimum_fraction_digits` | integer | no |  | Optional: at least this many decimal places. |
| `maximum_fraction_digits` | integer | no |  | Optional: at most this many decimal places (rounded). |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `formatted` | string |  |
| `currency` | string |  |

### Parse number (`parse_number`)

Read a number typed the way a locale writes it: "1.234,56" in de-DE and "1,234.56" in en-US are both 1234.56. Handles currency symbols and codes, percent (12% → 0.12), brackets and minus signs, and local digits.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  | The number as text. |
| `locale` | string | no | `"en-US"` | BCP 47 locale, e.g. en-US, en-NZ, de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | number | The number (empty when the text is not a number). |
| `valid` | boolean | Whether the text could be read as a number. |
| `decimal_separator` | string | The locale's decimal separator. |
| `group_separator` | string | The locale's thousands separator. |

### Format phone (`format_phone`)

Normalise a phone number to E.164 (+64211234567), or format it in international (+64 21 123 4567) or national (021 123 4567) style with simple grouping. North American numbers use (415) 555-0132.

**Inputs**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | string | yes |  | As typed: with + and country code, or national with Country set. |
| `country` | string | no |  | ISO country (NZ, US, GB, …) or calling code (64) for numbers without +. |
| `format` | choice: `e164`, `international`, `national` | no | `"international"` | Output style. |

**Outputs**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `formatted` | string | Empty when the number is not valid. |
| `e164` | string |  |
| `valid` | boolean |  |
| `reason` | string | Why the number is invalid (empty when valid). |

## Capabilities

None: pure computation. Locale data comes from the host's ctx.intl helpers (Unicode CLDR); the action cannot reach the network, data tables, files or secrets.

## Examples

**UK IBAN** (`validate`)

```json
{
  "type": "iban",
  "value": "GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32"
}
```

**Card number with issuer** (`validate`)

```json
{
  "type": "card",
  "value": "4111 1111 1111 1111"
}
```

**Onboarding form fields** (`validate_many`)

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "name": "Email",
      "type": "email",
      "value": "ap@example.co.nz"
    },
    {
      "name": "Bank",
      "type": "iban",
      "value": "DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00"
    },
    {
      "name": "Phone",
      "type": "phone",
      "value": "021 123 4567",
      "country": "NZ"
    },
    {
      "name": "Postcode",
      "type": "postcode",
      "value": "sw1a1aa",
      "country": "GB"
    }
  ]
}
```

**German amount to a number** (`parse_number`)

```json
{
  "text": "1.234,56 €",
  "locale": "de-DE"
}
```

**Yen without decimals** (`format_currency`)

```json
{
  "value": 1234567.8,
  "currency": "JPY",
  "locale": "ja-JP"
}
```

A sample workflow ships in `assets/workflows/`: it starts from the API or its start form, runs this action with default inputs and shows the outputs.

## Limits

- Each run has 5 seconds and 32 MB of sandbox memory; inputs and outputs are limited to 5 MB of JSON each.
- Checks prove a value is well-formed (format and check digits), not that an account, card, mailbox or person exists.
- Postcodes: US, GB, CA, AU, NZ, DE, FR, NL, BE, AT, CH, IE, ES, IT, PT, SE, NO, DK, FI, PL, JP, IN, SG, BR, MX, ZA.
- National IDs: us_ssn, uk_nino, ca_sin, au_tfn, nz_ird, nz_nhi, de_tax_id, fr_nir, es_dni, it_fiscal_code, nl_bsn, in_aadhaar, sg_nric (check digits as published by each issuer; the shared validators in lib/documents/pii/validators.ts).
- Phone numbers: E.164 allows 8–15 digits including the country code; national and international formats use simple grouping, not every country's own numbering plan.
- Validate many takes up to 10,000 entries.

## Build and test

```sh
node gallery/actions/scripts/build.mjs validation-formatting
npx vitest run __tests__/gallery-action-validation-formatting.test.ts
```

## Licence

Apache-2.0. Copyright UserTasks.
